question: Why should you look farther ahead on a freeway than on a city street?
options: a:Because it helps you keep up with traffic.,b:Because it takes a quarter of a mile to stop.,c:To see potential hazards earlier and allow more time to react.
note: Higher speeds on freeways require earlier detection of changing conditions and hazards.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim their headlights, what should you do?
options: a:Look straight ahead.,b:Look toward the center of the roadway.,c:Look toward the right side of the road to avoid glare.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded while keeping enough view to stay in your lane.

question: When following a motorcycle, what should you do?
options: a:Tailgate to prevent lane changes.,b:Drive more slowly than usual.,c:Be ready to use your horn frequently.,d:Allow a larger following distance (three to four seconds).
note: Maintain a larger following distance behind motorcycles because they can stop quickly and are more vulnerable in a fall.

question: If a lane-control sign over your lane has an arrow with 'ONLY' below it, you must:
options: a:Travel in the direction of the arrow.,b:Always make a lane change.,c:Look for a destination sign to follow.
note: A lane-control sign marked 'ONLY' indicates the required direction of travel for that lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is a U-turn prohibited?
options: a:In a parking lot.,b:At an intersection controlled by a stop sign.,c:On a straight road with 500 feet of clear view.,d:On or near any curve or hill.
note: Never make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill where you cannot clearly see approaching traffic; it creates a collision risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are collisions more likely to occur regarding vehicle speeds?
options: a:When all vehicles travel at about the same speed.,b:When one vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.,c:Only when vehicles travel too fast.,d:Only when vehicles travel too slowly.
note: Collisions are more likely when a vehicle's speed differs significantly from the general flow of traffic.

question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?
options: a:They are smaller and more difficult to see than adults.,b:They do not have the same physical reflexes as adults.,c:Both of the above.
note: Children are less predictable and harder to see; give extra space near schools, parks, and driveways.

question: If a pedestrian is partway across when your signal turns green, how should you proceed?
options: a:Wait until the pedestrian has cleared the street before you proceed.,b:Proceed if you have the right-of-way.,c:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
note: Yield to pedestrians in the intersection even if your light turns green; wait until they finish crossing.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline allow drivers to do?
options: a:Pass on the left when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing is not permitted.,c:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: Broken yellow centerlines permit passing on the left from the side with the dashed line when safe to do so.

question: Before returning to your lane after passing, what should you verify?
options: a:Flash your headlights.,b:Beep your horn.,c:See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: After passing, make sure you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror before moving back into that lane.

question: What term is used to describe the amount of alcohol in a person's blood?
options: a:Implied consent (IC).,b:Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).,c:Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).
note: BAC measures the percentage of alcohol in the bloodstream and is used to determine impairment.

question: Where is the safest place for children age 12 and under in a vehicle with airbags?
options: a:The front passenger seat.,b:Standing between the front seats.,c:The back seat.,d:The truck bed of a pickup.
note: Airbags can injure children; anyone age 12 or younger should ride in the back seat.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic control signal is not working, how should you proceed at the intersection?
options: a:If the intersection is clear,b:Drive quickly through the intersection to get out of the way of other vehicles.,c:Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.
note: Treat an unlit or nonworking signal as an all-way stop: stop, observe, and yield before entering.

question: What is the correct response to a tire blowout while driving?
options: a:Turn the steering wheel sharply to the side of the blowout.,b:Slow down gradually and use brakes lightly after speed drops.,c:Tap or pump the brakes repeatedly.,d:Apply the brakes firmly and stop immediately.
note: If a tire blows out, take your foot off the accelerator to slow, avoid heavy braking until slowed, and steer straight until you can pull off safely.

question: On a roadway with a single broken white centerline, what is permitted?
options: a:You may cross the centerline to change lanes.,b:You may change lanes only from the left lane.,c:You must stay within your lane.
note: Broken white lines separate same-direction lanes and allow lane changes when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, to whom must you yield?
options: a:Whoever arrived before you.,b:The driver on your left.,c:The driver across from your vehicle.
note: Vehicles proceed through a four-way stop in the order of arrival; yield to drivers who arrived before you.

question: If you become drowsy while driving, what is the best action?
options: a:Take a break.,b:Take some caffeine pills.,c:Try to fight it.
note: If tired, pull off at the next safe location to rest, nap, or change drivers; caffeine and pills are not reliable substitutes for sleep.

question: When is reaction time slowed?
options: a:After sleeping.,b:Only when driving at high speeds.,c:After drinking alcohol.,d:After working hard.
note: Alcohol slows reflexes and reaction time, impairing driving skills and judgment.

question: What type of drug is alcohol classified as?
options: a:A hallucinogen.,b:A depressant.,c:A stimulant.,d:An antihistamine.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that dulls judgment and slows reflexes, making driving unsafe.

question: Which statement about blind spots is true?
options: a:You can check blind spots using only your rearview mirror.,b:Blind spots are eliminated if you have one outside mirror.,c:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,d:Mirrors remove the need to look over your shoulder.
note: Even with proper mirrors, blind spots remain; large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger cars.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are already in an intersection when a green signal turns yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Stop immediately.,b:Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.,c:Increase your speed to get out quickly.
note: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, proceed through and clear it safely.

question: When a pedestrian is using a guide dog or carrying a white cane, how should you respond?
options: a:You only have to yield if you are at a corner.,b:You must tell them where to cross the street.,c:You must always yield the right-of-way.
note: Blind or partially blind pedestrians using a guide dog or white cane must always be given the right-of-way.

question: When changing lanes you should never do which of the following?
options: a:Change lanes abruptly or spontaneously.,b:Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane.,c:Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
note: Do not make sudden lane changes; always signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and ensure the lane is clear before moving.

question: When entering a freeway, check traffic by:
options: a:Assuming traffic will adjust for you.,b:Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.,c:Using only your rearview mirror.,d:Using your rearview and side mirrors.
note: When merging, use your side mirror and a shoulder check to ensure there is a safe gap in traffic before you merge into the freeway.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line indicate about passing?
options: a:Passing is allowed only during daylight.,b:Passing is allowed only for trucks.,c:Passing is allowed from the side with the broken line and prohibited from the solid side.,d:Passing is prohibited for both directions.
note: If the broken line is on your side, you may pass when safe; the solid-line side cannot pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate highway from an entrance ramp, what should you do?
options: a:Enter immediately and then adjust speed.,b:Reduce speed to 25 mph before merging.,c:Match the speed of traffic in the acceleration lane and merge when the way is clear.,d:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.
note: Use the acceleration lane to reach highway speed and merge smoothly with traffic when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You have entered a turn lane to make a left turn and there is oncoming traffic. What should you do?
options: a:Move to the left of the center lane.,b:Turn your front wheels to the left to be prepared to turn.,c:Signal before you arrive at the intersection.
note: Signal about 100 feet before the turn and keep your wheels straight until it is safe to start the left turn to avoid being pushed into oncoming traffic.

question: You may cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle only when which condition exists?
options: a:The vehicle in front signals for you to pass.,b:A broken yellow line is on the far side of the centerline.,c:There is a broken yellow line on your side of the centerline.,d:You are in a left-turn lane.
note: A broken yellow line next to your side of the road indicates you may pass when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-lane road, where is it illegal to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Both on a hill and in a curve.,b:On a hill only.,c:In a curve only.
note: Do not pass on hills or in curves where you cannot see oncoming traffic; only pass where it is safe and legal.

question: When you see pedestrians near the roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn and maintain your speed.,b:Slow down and pass with caution.,c:Speed up to clear the area quickly.
note: Slow and be prepared to stop for pedestrians; they may step into the roadway unexpectedly.

question: What dangerous outcome is most increased by driver fatigue?
options: a:Getting a parking ticket.,b:Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.,c:Being late for appointments.,d:Missing an exit.
note: Fatigue impairs decision-making and reaction time and can lead to falling asleep while driving, which greatly increases crash risk.

question: When should your wheels NOT be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.,b:When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.,c:When parked on the side of a level roadway where there is no curb.
note: When parked facing uphill or downhill, turn your wheels so the vehicle will not roll into traffic if the brakes fail.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Four-way flashers.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: Use low beams in fog, rain, or snow; high beams reflect and reduce visibility further.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are in the left of two lanes going your direction and others are passing on the right, what should you do?
options: a:Drive onto the left shoulder to let others pass.,b:Move into the right lane when it is safe.,c:Remain in the left lane regardless of traffic.,d:Increase your speed to stay ahead.
note: Use the left lane for passing or turning left; if you are impeding traffic, move right when safe.

question: To improve visibility in rain or fog, drivers should use which lights?
options: a:Parking lights only.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Hazard flashers only.,d:Low beam headlights.
note: Low beam headlights help visibility in rain, snow, sleet, or fog; high beams can reflect and reduce visibility.

question: When should you not use your horn?
options: a:When trying to move a slow driver along.,b:If you might hit another vehicle.,c:When visibility ahead is limited.,d:Near blind pedestrians.
note: Avoid using the horn near blind pedestrians as it may be dangerous; yield to them and proceed only when safe.

question: What shape and color are most temporary work zone signs?
options: a:Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.,b:Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.,c:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange background and black symbols.
note: Temporary construction or maintenance signs have orange backgrounds with black letters or symbols.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing?
options: a:After you pass the other vehicle’s front bumper.,b:Only after signaling three times.,c:When you can no longer see the vehicle,d:When you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
note: You should re-enter the lane only after being sure there is adequate space — typically when you can see the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what is the correct initial response?
options: a:Turn off the ignition.,b:Ease up on the gas pedal.,c:Brake as hard as possible.
note: Release the accelerator or brake to regain balance and steer into the direction of the skid to regain control.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian who uses a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Only when a crossing guard is present.,b:Only when the guide dog is leading the person across the street.,c:At all times.
note: Pedestrians with a guide dog or white cane must be given the right-of-way whenever they are crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a short interstate entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, how should you enter?
options: a:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a green signal.,b:Use the shoulder to get to highway speed before merging.,c:Immediately enter the far-right traffic lane and then speed up.,d:Speed up only after you identify a gap in traffic and then merge.
note: Without an acceleration lane, wait for a safe gap and then accelerate to merge with traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which behavior blocks the smooth flow of traffic?
options: a:Driving at the legal speed limit.,b:Slowing down to look at a collision scene (rubbernecking).,c:Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.,d:Using public transportation.
note: Rubbernecking—slowing to look at collisions—creates congestion and blocks the smooth flow of traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you begin a left turn from a multilane one-way street onto a one-way street?
options: a:The rightmost lane.,b:The lane closest to the left curb.,c:Any lane as long as it is safe.,d:The center lane only.
note: When turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, start from the far left lane.

question: At a crosswalk, who must yield?
options: a:Construction workers must yield to vehicles.,b:Cyclists always have priority over pedestrians.,c:Pedestrians must yield to vehicles.,d:Vehicles must yield to pedestrians.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks, marked or unmarked, unless directed otherwise by signals.

question: How close to a fire hydrant may you legally park?
options: a:You may not park within 25 feet of a fire hydrant.,b:You may not park within 30 feet of a fire hydrant.,c:You may not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.,d:You may park directly beside a hydrant if attended.
note: Parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant is prohibited to allow emergency access.

question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while you are driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Brake as hard as possible immediately.,b:Rapidly pump the brake pedal several times.,c:Turn sharply toward the shoulder.,d:Grip the steering wheel
note: If a tire blows out, hold the wheel firmly, let the vehicle slow by itself, and brake gently if needed before pulling over safely.

question: When parking uphill where there is no curb, how should you set your wheels?
options: a:Keep your wheels straight.,b:Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.,c:Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
note: On an uphill with no curb, turn wheels toward the road edge so the car will roll off the road instead of into traffic if brakes fail.

question: What are 'no zones' around large trucks?
options: a:Areas that provide sufficient space to travel behind the truck.,b:Areas with several car lengths between vehicles and the truck.,c:Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are so close they restrict the truck driver's ability to stop and maneuver safely.
note: 'No zones' are large blind spots where the truck driver cannot see other vehicles and where close positioning reduces the truck driver's ability to react.

question: What behavior is an example of defensive driving?
options: a:Driving with parking lights on during the day.,b:Only focusing on the vehicle directly in front of you.,c:Putting only one car length between you and the vehicle ahead.,d:Keeping your eyes moving to look for possible hazards.
note: Defensive driving involves scanning the road and monitoring surroundings to anticipate and avoid hazards.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal indicate?
options: a:You should speed up to beat the light.,b:You may turn without yielding to oncoming traffic.,c:The protected-turn phase is ending; be prepared to stop and yield.,d:Left turns are prohibited.
note: A solid yellow arrow warns that the green arrow is ending; if turning, yield to oncoming traffic and prepare to stop.

question: If you see pedestrians in an upcoming crosswalk, what should you do?
options: a:Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.,b:Pull to the right and go around the pedestrians.,c:Continue ahead; you have the right-of-way.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and should wait until they have cleared the roadway before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before you change lanes you should:
options: a:Slow down dramatically,b:Assume other drivers will make room.,c:Check only the inside rearview mirror.,d:Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
note: Always check side mirrors and perform a shoulder check to clear blind spots before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing another vehicle?
options: a:As soon as you are slightly ahead of the vehicle.,b:When the other driver waves you back in.,c:After you signal for three seconds.,d:When you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.
note: You should only return to your lane once you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror, ensuring a safe gap.

question: If the center of the road has one solid yellow and one broken yellow line with the broken line next to you, what does that mean?
options: a:You are in a passing zone and may pass on the left if no oncoming traffic is present.,b:You are only allowed to make right turns here.,c:You are not allowed to pass in this area.
note: When the broken line is next to your lane you may pass on the left if the way ahead is clear and safe.

question: When must you stop before crossing railroad tracks?
options: a:Only if you are transporting passengers.,b:When a traffic officer signals you to stop.,c:If there isn’t space on the far side to clear the tracks.,d:Only when the crossing is in a city or town.
note: Never stop on the tracks; if you cannot clear the far side, wait until there is room so your vehicle won't be trapped on the tracks.

question: How can you prevent becoming an aggressive driver?
options: a:Use your horn frequently to assert yourself.,b:Drive above the posted speed limit to avoid others.,c:Relax,d:Tailgate slower drivers to express frustration.
note: Stay calm, focus on safe driving, and be realistic about travel time to reduce aggressive responses.

question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, what must you be prepared for?
options: a:Change lanes and maintain your current speed.,b:Slow down because the lane ends ahead.,c:Be prepared for workers and slow equipment ahead.
note: Construction zones may have workers, slow equipment, and lane closures—reduce speed and be ready to stop.

question: As your speed increases, what becomes more important to do?
options: a:Change lanes frequently.,b:Follow the vehicle ahead more closely.,c:Turn on your headlights at all times.,d:Look well ahead of your vehicle to anticipate hazards.
note: Higher speeds require earlier scanning so you have more time to react to hazards and changes in traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach an intersection at the speed limit and the light turns yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection if you can safely do so.,b:Speed up to beat the red light.,c:Proceed through the intersection without caution.,d:Turn on your hazard lights and continue.
note: A steady yellow means the light is about to turn red; stop if you can do so safely, otherwise proceed cautiously.

question: What can speed up the elimination of alcohol from the body?
options: a:Eating a large meal.,b:Nothing. Only time will allow all alcohol to leave a person's system.,c:Taking a cold shower.
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize alcohol; coffee, showers, or food do not accelerate elimination.

question: If there is no marked crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, what should you do?
options: a:Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.,b:Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.,c:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway even if there is no marked crosswalk—stop and allow them to finish crossing.

question: What does double solid yellow centerline mean?
options: a:Passing allowed from the right only.,b:No passing allowed from either direction.,c:Passing allowed at intersections.,d:Passing allowed from the left only.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and indicate that passing is not permitted from either direction.

question: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down gradually and do not apply the brakes.,b:Speed up to regain contact with the road.,c:Turn the steering wheel sharply away from the skid.,d:Apply the brakes firmly to regain traction.
note: When hydroplaning, ease off the accelerator and let speed reduce; avoid braking which can worsen loss of control.

question: If your tires feel like they have lost contact with the road surface, you should:
options: a:Ease your foot off the gas pedal and avoid braking.,b:Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.,c:Turn the wheel sharply to regain traction.,d:Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.
note: If you begin to hydroplane or feel loss of traction, ease off the accelerator and avoid braking or turning until the tires regain contact.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To enter a gap in highway traffic safely, what should you do first?
options: a:Speed up and let the other vehicles make way.,b:Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.,c:Check behind you
note: Before merging or changing lanes, check behind and to the sides, then time your entry to match the gap in traffic.

question: A driver's license is considered a:
options: a:A requirement you must always carry.,b:Right,c:A guaranteed entitlement.,d:Privilege
note: A driver's license is a privilege granted by the state; it must be earned and can be suspended or revoked for violations.

question: Approaching a stopped school bus with flashing lights and an extended stop arm, drivers should:
options: a:Continue driving when they think the kids are done exiting the bus.,b:Honk their horn before passing the bus on its left.,c:Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
note: Stop and remain stopped until the bus retracts its stop arm, turns off flashing lights, and resumes motion.

question: Roadways marked with double solid yellow centerlines indicate what about passing?
options: a:Passing is allowed from both directions.,b:Passing is not allowed from either direction.,c:Allowed only from your direction of travel.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing from either direction because traffic moves in opposite directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must drivers turning left yield to?
options: a:Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right.,b:Only pedestrians in crosswalks.,c:No one if they have a green light.,d:Vehicles behind them attempting to pass.
note: Drivers making a left turn must yield to any approaching traffic from the opposite direction, including vehicles going straight or turning right.

question: Which statement about driving through roadwork zones is true?
options: a:You must slow down for the Cone Zone and be prepared to stop.,b:You can ignore temporary signs if you know the road.,c:You may speed through if no workers are visible.,d:Fines for violations are the same as under normal conditions.
note: Reduce speed and drive carefully through work zones to protect workers and other road users; 'Slow for the Cone Zone.'

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, you should enter at what speed?
options: a:At the legal speed limit regardless of traffic.,b:More slowly than the freeway traffic.,c:At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.
note: Merge at or near the speed of existing freeway traffic so you can blend smoothly into the flow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is close enough to cause a conflict.,b:Slow down but never stop.,c:Yield only to vehicles on your right.
note: At a yield sign, slow or stop if necessary and give way to traffic or pedestrians that could cause a collision.

question: At about what speed can a car begin to hydroplane on standing water?
options: a:45 miles per hour.,b:Around 35 miles per hour.,c:60 miles per hour.,d:20 miles per hour.
note: Hydroplaning can begin at speeds near 35 mph; as speed increases tires may lose contact with the road.

question: Why is night driving more hazardous?
options: a:Distance and speed of other vehicles are harder to judge in the dark.,b:The speed limit is increased at night.,c:There are always fewer vehicles at night.,d:Headlights make it safer so it's not hazardous.
note: Reduced visibility at night makes it difficult to judge distance and speed; you can only see as far as your headlights allow.

question: As you near the crest of a hill, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up slightly.,b:Maintain a steady speed regardless of conditions.,c:Prepare to stop if needed and adjust speed.
note: You cannot see beyond the hill; reduce speed and be ready to stop for hazards hidden from view.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these commonly contributes to traffic crashes?
options: a:Constantly scanning the environment.,b:Getting adequate rest and staying alert.,c:Exceeding posted speed limits and driving too fast for conditions.,d:Driving at the exact same speed as surrounding traffic.
note: Driving over the speed limit or too fast for conditions frequently contributes to crashes.

question: Why use headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?
options: a:To warn others of bad weather conditions.,b:To keep your engine warm.,c:So others can see your vehicle.
note: Headlights make your vehicle more visible to other drivers during precipitation or reduced visibility; use low beams when wipers are needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to make a left turn on red after stopping?
options: a:Only when you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street and signs don't prohibit it.,b:When traveling on a two-way street and turning onto a two-way street.,c:Whenever you yield to all other traffic at the intersection.
note: Left on red is allowed only from one one-way street onto another after a full stop and when not prohibited by signs.

question: When are streets and highways most slippery?
options: a:When they are clean and dry.,b:Just after it starts to rain.,c:When it has been raining hard for several hours.
note: Road surfaces are especially slippery during the first half hour of rain as water mixes with oils and debris on the pavement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To see objects in your blind spot when changing lanes, drivers should check:
options: a:Over their left or right shoulder.,b:Only the inside rearview mirror.,c:Only the left outside mirror.,d:Only the backup camera.
note: Looking over the appropriate shoulder reveals areas hidden from mirrors and helps ensure safe lane changes.

question: If a driver is following you too closely on a two-lane road, you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to drive around you.,b:Speed up to increase the distance from the tailgater.,c:Apply your brakes to slow down,d:Stop suddenly to warn them.
note: If you are being tailgated, change lanes if possible; if not, gradually slow down to encourage the tailgater to pass rather than speeding up or braking abruptly.

question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, what should you expect?
options: a:Sound your horn to warn them.,b:They will maintain a perfectly straight line.,c:Expect the unexpected and be prepared to react.,d:The child will always obey traffic rules.
note: Children on bicycles can be unpredictable; slow down and be ready for sudden moves.

question: If a vehicle has airbags, how should seat belts be used?
options: a:Seat belts do not need to be worn.,b:Seat belts should be worn behind the back.,c:Seat belts should still be worn.
note: Airbags supplement seat belts; for best protection, always use lap and shoulder belts in combination with airbags.

question: What must you do when you encounter an octagonal sign?
options: a:Slow.,b:Turn.,c:Stop.
note: An eight-sided sign always means 'Stop'—come to a complete stop and yield if necessary.

question: Before backing up your vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Flash your high beams to alert others.,b:Rev your engine to warn pedestrians.,c:Close all windows and lock doors.,d:Walk around your vehicle to ensure no person or obstacle is behind it.
note: Before reversing, walk around your vehicle to check for people or objects, then look over your shoulder while backing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action is never allowed when you want to change lanes?
options: a:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,b:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.,c:Move into another lane while within an intersection.,d:Use your turn signal before changing lanes.
note: Never change lanes while inside an intersection; always check mirrors and blind spots before moving.

question: When merging onto the interstate after accelerating and signaling, you should:
options: a:Wait for the entire lane to clear before merging.,b:Stop on the acceleration lane if no gap appears.,c:Merge carefully into the gap.,d:Expect traffic to allow you to proceed because you have the right-of-way.
note: Identify a gap, match the speed of traffic, signal, and merge carefully when it is safe; do not assume other drivers will make room.

question: Which statement best describes backing a vehicle?
options: a:Backing is only dangerous when a helper is present.,b:Backing is safe if you only use mirrors.,c:Backing is only risky in large vehicles.,d:Backing is always risky because you have limited rear visibility.
note: Reversing is hazardous due to limited visibility; use extra caution, look out the rear window, and use assistance when available.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should not enter an intersection if doing so will block it when the light turns red:
options: a:Under any circumstances.,b:Only if directed by a police officer.,c:Unless you entered the intersection on a green light.,d:Unless you entered the intersection on a yellow light.
note: Never enter an intersection unless you can clear it completely; blocking intersections is illegal even if the light is green when you enter.

question: How can you help the driver behind you keep a safe following distance?
options: a:Maintain a steady speed.,b:Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.,c:Brake abruptly to get their attention.,d:Flash your lights frequently.
note: Maintaining a steady speed and signaling in advance helps the driver behind you keep a safe distance.

question: If you are getting tired while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Drink something with caffeine.,b:Open a window.,c:Stop and either get rest or change drivers.
note: If fatigue sets in, pull over at a safe location to rest, nap, or switch drivers; caffeine is not a reliable substitute for sleep.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must drivers obey at a construction site directing traffic?
options: a:Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.,b:Security guards in parking lots.,c:Other drivers with broken-down vehicles.,d:Construction workers off the roadway only.
note: Drivers must obey instructions from flaggers; they direct traffic to keep drivers and workers safe.

question: After drinking several beers, what is the only effective way to reduce alcohol's effects?
options: a:Drink several cups of coffee.,b:Wait; allow time for the body to eliminate the alcohol.,c:Take a cold shower.
note: Time is the only way to lower BAC; coffee, showers, or exercise do not speed elimination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do if an emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing red or blue lights?
options: a:Continue driving but try to stay out of its way.,b:Pull over to the side of the road and come to a complete stop.,c:Speed up to pass it quickly.,d:Try to reach your destination before it catches up to you.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights, you must pull over to the right and stop until it has passed.

question: If a child appears about to run into the street, you should:
options: a:Sound a sharp blast of your horn.,b:Begin to prepare to slow down.,c:Flash your headlights.,d:Swerve sharply into the next lane.
note: If there is an immediate danger, give a sharp blast on your horn to warn the child and other pedestrians; take appropriate braking action after warning.

question: What should you do when driving in work zones?
options: a:Maintain your normal speed the whole way through the zone.,b:Increase your speed to get through quickly.,c:Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop suddenly.
note: Slow down, obey posted signs, and be prepared to stop—workers and changed lane patterns may be present.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line indicate?
options: a:Passing is prohibited from both directions.,b:Traffic next to the broken line may pass; traffic next to the solid line may not.,c:Passing is allowed only at intersections.,d:Both lanes may pass whenever safe.
note: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line means drivers next to the broken line may pass, but those next to the solid line may not.

question: If you are in an intersection and an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights and siren, what should you do?
options: a:Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.,b:Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.,c:Continue through the intersection
note: If in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches, clear the intersection, then move to the right and stop to yield.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors while driving?
options: a:To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.,b:Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.,c:Only when you are slowing down.
note: Frequently check mirrors to maintain awareness of traffic around you—every 2–5 seconds is recommended.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is a common effect of excessive speed on driving behavior?
options: a:It does not increase crash risk.,b:It conserves fuel on long trips.,c:It often leads to risky decision-making.,d:It increases your ability to react to hazards.
note: High speed reduces reaction time and often results in dangerous choices and more severe collisions.

question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.,b:After about three seconds no matter what.,c:When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,d:When you hear the overtaken vehicle's engine rev.
note: Return to your lane only after you can see the passed vehicle's entire front in your rearview mirror, and always check blind spots first.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:Only if the pedestrian is on the sidewalk.,b:Only when pedestrians are within marked crosswalks.,c:Only if the pedestrian signals you.,d:At all times.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and whenever necessary to avoid striking a pedestrian.

question: When bicycles are used on roadways, they are considered:
options: a:Pedestrians for traffic law purposes.,b:Hazards that must yield to cars.,c:Illegal on all roadways.,d:Vehicles and must follow the same rules of the road.
note: On roadways, bicycles are legally vehicles and cyclists must obey the same traffic laws as motorists.

question: At a red light with a green arrow, when may you proceed in the arrow's direction?
options: a:Only when a police officer signals you to go.,b:Only after coming to a complete stop first.,c:Only if the arrow turns green again after the red.,d:When you are in the proper lane and the way is clear.
note: A green arrow gives protected movement in that direction; proceed from the correct lane when the way is clear.

question: On a multilane road, what does a dashed yellow next to a solid yellow line mean?
options: a:Passing is permitted from both directions.,b:Passing is permitted only from the direction next to the dashed line.,c:Passing is prohibited from both directions.
note: Only traffic adjacent to the dashed yellow line may pass; traffic next to the solid yellow line may not.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, what is the correct immediate action?
options: a:Brake hard and steer sharply toward the right edge of the roadway.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly.,c:Grip the steering wheel firmly
note: Keep control by holding the wheel, easing off the gas, and slowing gently before moving off the roadway.

question: What is true about bicycles on the roadway?
options: a:They are restricted to sidewalks only.,b:They must always yield to motor vehicles.,c:They are vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.,d:They do not follow road rules.
note: Bicycles on the road are considered vehicles and have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you plan to pass another vehicle, what should you not assume?
options: a:That they will allow you to pass if you signal.,b:That they will maintain a constant speed.,c:That the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.
note: Never assume the other driver will create space; only pass when you have sufficient room and it is safe.

question: What does a green arrow on a traffic signal require you to do?
options: a:Yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection, then proceed in arrow direction.,b:Proceed immediately without checking for pedestrians.,c:Wait four seconds before proceeding.,d:Stop until the arrow turns off.
note: A green arrow means you may go in the arrow's direction after yielding to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

question: What is the only effective method to remove alcohol from the body?
options: a:Drink strong coffee.,b:Wait; allow time for the body to metabolize alcohol.,c:Take a cold shower.
note: Only time will lower BAC and remove alcohol from your system; other remedies do not work.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is NOT a safe practice on an interstate?
options: a:Change lanes without signaling.,b:Slower traffic must keep to the right.,c:If you miss your exit
note: Always signal lane changes and follow posted rules; changing lanes without signaling is unsafe and illegal.

question: What does a yellow pennant-shaped sign indicate?
options: a:No passing zone.,b:Right turns only.,c:Right turns permitted.
note: A pennant-shaped yellow sign indicates the start of a no-passing zone for drivers.

question: To reduce the chance of skidding on slippery surfaces, you should:
options: a:Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.,b:Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.,c:Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
note: Slow before curves and intersections on slippery roads; braking on a curve can cause a skid.

question: What should a driver watch while operating a vehicle?
options: a:Ahead,b:Only directly in front of the vehicle.,c:The dashboard instruments exclusively.,d:Only the rearview mirror.
note: Good drivers continuously scan all around the vehicle to detect potential hazards early.

question: If the rear of your car begins skidding left, what steering action should you take?
options: a:Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.,b:Steer left to recover alignment.,c:Steer right immediately.,d:Apply the parking brake.
note: In a skid you should remove your foot from the brake and steer in the direction you want to go; if the rear skids left, steer left to straighten the vehicle.

question: When traveling at high speeds, how long before a lane change or turn should you signal?
options: a:One second.,b:Four to five seconds.,c:Two to three seconds.
note: At higher speeds you should signal earlier—about four to five seconds—to warn others of your intent.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning on wet roads?
options: a:Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it starts to rain.,b:Slow down.,c:Put on your cruise control to maintain a constant speed.
note: Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on water; reducing speed on wet pavement lowers the chance of hydroplaning.

question: Is it legal to have open containers of alcohol while in a motor vehicle on a highway?
options: a:Yes — passengers may drink but drivers may not.,b:Yes — as long as the vehicle is not moving.,c:Only if you are under 21.,d:No — it is illegal to drink from or possess open containers while in operation.
note: Open containers and drinking alcohol in a vehicle on a highway are prohibited; drivers and passengers may face penalties.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are repeatedly being passed while driving in the center lane of an expressway, what should you do?
options: a:Increase your speed to match the fastest cars.,b:Move to the left lane immediately.,c:Stay in the center lane regardless.,d:Move to the right lane when it is safe.
note: On multi-lane highways, use right lanes for slower travel and leave left lanes for passing or faster traffic.

question: A school bus ahead in your lane is stopped with red lights flashing. You should:
options: a:Stop and proceed when you believe all children have exited.,b:Pass if you see no children nearby.,c:Slow to 25 mph and pass cautiously.,d:Stop and remain stopped while the red lights are flashing.
note: When a school bus is using flashing red lights, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing; exceptions apply on divided highways.

question: If you hit a parked car and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Leave a note with your name and address on the vehicle.,b:Call your insurance company when you get home.,c:Wait for the owner to return.
note: If you hit unattended property, leave a note with contact details and notify authorities if required.

question: Why is using a cell phone while driving considered a distraction?
options: a:It causes the driver to worry about the cost of the call.,b:It draws the attention of other drivers.,c:It occupies the driver's hands
note: Using a phone while driving takes away the driver's hands, eyes, and attention, increasing crash risk.

question: How should you check for vehicles in your blind spots?
options: a:Use only the inside rearview mirror.,b:Only use the outside rearview mirror.,c:Check over your shoulders.
note: Blind spots are not visible through mirrors—look over your shoulder to confirm the lane you intend to enter is clear.

question: You exit the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill. What should you do before the curve?
options: a:Slow to a safe speed before entering the curve.,b:Wait until you are in the curve to begin braking.,c:Maintain freeway speed until the curve is complete.,d:Increase speed to avoid holding up traffic.
note: Always slow to a safe speed before a downhill curved ramp; braking in a curve can cause skids.

question: When a school bus ahead on your side of the road has flashing red lights, you must:
options: a:Change lanes and pass the bus.,b:Proceed at normal speed if you see no children.,c:Stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing.,d:Slow down to 10 mph and pass cautiously.
note: You must stop for a school bus loading or unloading children when its red lights flash and stop arm is out.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it ever legal to drive off the road onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle?
options: a:If the vehicle ahead is turning left.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:If there are two or more lanes in your direction.,d:If the shoulder is wide enough and clear.
note: You may not drive off the paved or main-traveled portion of the roadway onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do regarding the brakes?
options: a:Apply the brakes lightly immediately.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly.,c:Stay off the brakes and steer to regain control.
note: If you skid, avoid braking abruptly—steer smoothly to regain control and let the vehicle slow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your view to the side is blocked at an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Run the light quickly to avoid delay.,b:Stop,c:Honk and proceed slowly without stopping.,d:Maintain your speed and look both ways.
note: If your view is obstructed, stop and creep forward slowly until you can see clearly in both directions before proceeding.

question: If stopping on snow or ice and your vehicle has ABS, you should:
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,c:Stay off the brakes and let the car drift to a stop.,d:Use the parking brake instead of the foot brake.
note: Vehicles with ABS require you to press and hold the brake pedal firmly; the system will modulate braking for you.

question: Which statement about blind spots is correct?
options: a:You can see all blind spots using rearview mirrors.,b:Blind spots don't exist for small cars.,c:They are eliminated if you have one outside mirror on each side.,d:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
note: Blind spots are areas not visible in mirrors; large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger cars.

question: Which is true about driving after taking medications?
options: a:Many over-the-counter cold medicines can cause drowsiness and impair driving.,b:All over-the-counter medicines are safe at recommended doses.,c:Prescription medications never impair driving if prescribed by a doctor.,d:Medications cannot affect experienced drivers.
note: Over-the-counter and prescription medications can impair alertness and reaction time; know how yours affects you.

question: At dawn, dusk, or during rain or snow, which lights help other drivers see you best?
options: a:Turn up the instrument panel lights.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Turn on your parking lights.
note: Use your headlights when visibility is reduced. If windshield wipers are required, low beam headlights must also be used.

question: How many alcoholic drinks are required to affect driving ability?
options: a:It takes at least two drinks.,b:Alcohol has no effect if eaten with food.,c:Even one drink can impair driving.,d:Three drinks are required to impair driving.
note: Even a single alcoholic drink can affect coordination and judgment and make driving unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer is directing traffic at a lighted intersection, whose instructions do you follow?
options: a:Honk at the officer.,b:Follow the directions indicated by the traffic light.,c:Follow the directions given by the officer.
note: Drivers must obey directions from a police officer directing traffic even if they conflict with traffic signals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle is using its siren and flashing lights?
options: a:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.,b:Continue at the same speed and stay in your lane.,c:Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop.,d:Stop immediately even if you are inside an intersection.
note: You must yield to any emergency vehicle using a siren and flashing lights by driving to the right edge of the road and stopping; do not stop in an intersection. Resume driving after it has passed.

question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, how should you respond?
options: a:Make eye contact with and then pass the pedestrian.,b:Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.,c:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing the street.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing the roadway, even when there is no marked crosswalk.

question: When must you use your low beam headlights?
options: a:When in fog, snow, rain, or other conditions that reduce visibility.,b:Only on unlit roads.,c:Only when another vehicle is approaching.,d:When parked on the shoulder at night.
note: Use low beams any time visibility is reduced by fog, rain, snow, or mist; high beams can reflect and worsen visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a curve, when should you slow down?
options: a:In the middle of the curve.,b:After you have completed the curve.,c:Before entering the curve.,d:Only if a sign indicates to do so.
note: Reduce speed before you start the curve to avoid losing traction or control while turning.

question: For drivers age 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a BAC of at least what percent?
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: Drivers 21+ are legally impaired at 0.08% BAC or higher and face criminal penalties for DUI.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, how should you wear it?
options: a:Use only the shoulder belt.,b:Use only the lap belt.,c:Use both the lap and shoulder belts.,d:Wear the shoulder belt behind your back.
note: Both lap and shoulder belts must be worn together for maximum protection; wearing only one reduces effectiveness.

question: When driving at night, what is a recommended safety practice?
options: a:Look directly at oncoming headlights.,b:Always use high beams.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: At night, increase following distance and use proper light settings; avoid staring at oncoming lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you cannot find a gap to enter the freeway, what should you do on the ramp?
options: a:Slow down on the ramp and wait for a safe gap.,b:Back up on the ramp to a merge point.,c:Maintain your speed and force others to make room.,d:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for traffic to clear.
note: If you don't see a gap to merge into traffic, slow on the ramp and wait for a safe opening rather than stopping at the ramp end.

question: Which behavior may identify an aggressive driver?
options: a:Erratic and improper lane changes.,b:Driving very slowly.,c:The number of passengers in the vehicle.
note: Aggressive drivers often make sudden, unsafe lane changes; avoid challenging them and give them space.

question: When parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn the front wheels?
options: a:Leave the wheels unlocked so they can roll.,b:Turn them straight ahead.,c:Turn them to the right,d:Turn them left toward the center of the road.
note: On hills without a curb, turn your wheels so the vehicle would roll away from the center of the road if the brakes fail (toward the side of the road).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings you should always:
options: a:Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason.,b:Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.,c:Stop, listen, and proceed cautiously.
note: Always scan left and right at places where people or other vehicles may enter your path to ensure safety.

question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, which headlight setting is appropriate?
options: a:Use high beams until you are 10 feet behind the car.,b:Keep your headlights on low beam.,c:Turn off your headlights to avoid glare.,d:Use high beams regardless of surrounding vehicles.
note: Lower beams are required when following another vehicle closely to avoid blinding the driver ahead.

question: Why should you signal continuously while making a turn?
options: a:Because it's illegal to switch it off before finishing the turn.,b:It tells other road users your intentions.,c:Because it is always unsafe to turn off a signal early.
note: Continuous signaling communicates your intended maneuvers to drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians.

question: To whom should you give the right-of-way?
options: a:Only to pedestrians crossing any street.,b:In a marked crosswalk only.,c:In any crosswalk or intersection.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in marked and unmarked crosswalks and intersections.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can you make room for cars entering the freeway?
options: a:Drive onto the shoulder to let them in.,b:Maintain your speed and position at all times.,c:Merge into another lane when safe or slow down to create space.,d:Speed up to prevent them from merging.
note: If safe, change lanes or adjust speed to create a gap for entering traffic.

question: What is a crosswalk?
options: a:The area designated for pedestrian crossing the roadway.,b:Another name for a four-way intersection.,c:A zone for road construction workers only.,d:An area where bicycles must dismount.
note: A crosswalk is the area where pedestrians are expected to cross; it may be marked or unmarked and still has legal protection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left at a corner, to whom must you yield?
options: a:All approaching vehicles regardless of direction.,b:Only motorists turning right.,c:Pedestrians and oncoming traffic as required.,d:Only vehicles traveling slower than you.
note: Yield to pedestrians and oncoming vehicles who have the right-of-way before making a left turn.

question: After a collision, what is the safest guideline about moving injured people?
options: a:Move injured people as far from the road as possible.,b:Avoid moving the injured unless absolutely necessary.,c:Immediately transport injured persons yourself.,d:Insist that injured people are fine without medical aid.
note: Do not move injured persons unless they are in immediate danger (fire, traffic); wait for trained medical help.

question: Alcohol in any concentration is classified as a:
options: a:Neutral substance.,b:Stimulant.,c:Depressant.,d:Hallucinogen.
note: Alcohol depresses the central nervous system, slowing reactions and impairing judgment and coordination.

question: What best describes a driving distraction?
options: a:Anything that forces you to pay more attention to driving.,b:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,c:Listening to the radio at a moderate volume.,d:Only using a mobile phone while driving.
note: A distraction is any activity that diverts eyes, hands, or mind from driving tasks and increases crash risk.

question: When stopped behind a school bus with red lights flashing, when may you proceed?
options: a:The stop arm is retracted.,b:All students are off the bus.,c:The stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.
note: You must remain stopped until the bus turns off its flashing red lights, retracts the stop arm, and begins to move.

question: What is the best general way to avoid dangerous situations while driving?
options: a:Know what is happening around your vehicle by scanning front,b:Keep your eyes focused only ahead of the car.,c:Turn off the radio.
note: Constantly observe your surroundings to detect hazards early and take appropriate action.

question: What does a diamond-shaped road sign indicate?
options: a:Warning.,b:Stop.,c:Yield.
note: Diamond-shaped signs warn of special conditions or hazards ahead and are typically yellow or orange.

question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn and you also need to turn right, what should you do?
options: a:Squeeze between the truck/bus and the curb to get through.,b:Wait until the truck or bus has completed its turn before you turn.,c:Quickly turn before the truck or bus can.
note: Large vehicles need extra space to complete turns; wait until they finish rather than squeezing by.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should the maximum posted speed limit be driven?
options: a:During the night.,b:During the day.,c:Only under ideal road and weather conditions.
note: The posted maximum speed is for ideal conditions; adjust downward for weather, traffic, or poor visibility.

question: At what speed should you approach a blind intersection?
options: a:No faster than 30 mph.,b:At the posted speed limit.,c:No faster than 20 mph.,d:No faster than 15 mph.
note: When visibility is blocked by trees, buildings, or foliage, reduce speed to 15 mph or less when approaching the intersection.

question: If dust or smoke reduces visibility, what lights should you switch on?
options: a:Headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:Emergency flashers only.,d:Interior dome light.
note: Turn on your headlights whenever conditions prevent you from seeing other vehicles so other drivers can see you as well.

question: For quick, controlled steering turns, how should your hands be positioned on the wheel?
options: a:On opposite sides of the steering wheel.,b:Next to each other on the top of the steering wheel.,c:On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.
note: Place both hands on opposite sides of the wheel for secure control and safe turning.

question: If your lane has a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line, which vehicles may pass?
options: a:Vehicles next to the solid line may pass.,b:Vehicles in both directions may pass.,c:Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
note: A broken yellow line next to your lane means drivers adjacent to the broken line may pass when safe; the solid-side drivers may not.

question: What should you do before turning the ignition on?
options: a:Buckle your safety belt.,b:Be sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.,c:Buckle your safety belt and ensure all passengers have buckled theirs.
note: Develop a routine: before switching on the ignition, fasten your seatbelt and verify passengers are secured.

question: What do "No passing zone" signs tell drivers?
options: a:To speed up slightly to pass quickly.,b:That passing is allowed only during daylight.,c:That it is not safe or legal to pass in the indicated area.,d:To maintain a steady speed while passing.
note: A "No passing zone" sign indicates a section of road where passing is not safe or permitted.

question: How must you treat a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:Wait until it turns green.,b:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:You are traveling the wrong way.,d:As if it were a stop sign (come to a full stop and proceed when safe).
note: A flashing red light requires a complete stop; proceed only when it is safe and after yielding right-of-way.

question: At a railroad crossing, what must you be aware of?
options: a:That crossings are always safe after one train passes.,b:That gates always function correctly.,c:Only the train that just passed.,d:Vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings and the possibility of multiple trains.
note: Approach crossings with caution, watch for vehicles that must stop (school buses, hazardous material trucks), and be alert for multiple trains.

question: How can you keep track of traffic behind you?
options: a:Frequently check your rearview mirror.,b:Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots at all times.,c:Rely only on your side mirrors.,d:Turn and look out your back window.
note: Check your rearview mirror often to maintain awareness of traffic behind you; supplement with side checks when changing lanes.

question: When you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop every time.,c:Maintain your normal speed.,d:Yield only if other vehicles are present.
note: A flashing yellow signal means proceed with caution after slowing; it does not require a complete stop unless necessary for safety.

question: If you approach a stopped school bus with flashing lights and extended stop arm, you must:
options: a:Change lanes and pass cautiously.,b:Pass at 15 mph if no children are visible.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the bus resumes motion.,d:Proceed at normal speed while watching for children.
note: When a school bus is stopped with signals active, all drivers must stop until the lights and arm are withdrawn.

question: What does a curb painted red signify?
options: a:A loading zone during business hours.,b:A zone reserved for quick passenger drop-offs.,c:Accessible parking only.,d:No stopping
note: A red-painted curb means stopping, standing, or parking is prohibited at that location.

question: After it first starts to rain and the road becomes slippery, what should you do?
options: a:Test your tires' traction while driving uphill.,b:Avoid making fast turns or stopping at high speeds.,c:Decrease the distance you look ahead of your vehicle.
note: Roads are most slippery just after rain begins; reduce speed and avoid sudden turns or stops to lower the risk of skidding.

question: Why increase your following distance behind a large truck or bus?
options: a:To get caught in the vehicle's slipstream.,b:To see around the sides of the vehicle and because the driver may not see you.,c:Because other drivers tend to pull behind large vehicles before passing them.
note: Large vehicles can block your view and their drivers may have limited visibility of you—leave extra space.

question: What is a likely effect of combining prescription drugs with alcohol?
options: a:It reduces the risk of impairment.,b:There will likely be no effect.,c:It can make you unfit to drive.,d:It makes you more alert.
note: Many medications can impair driving; combining them with alcohol often increases drowsiness and decreases coordination.

question: Who is required to wear a safety belt in a moving vehicle?
options: a:All of the vehicle's occupants.,b:Only children,c:Just the driver
note: Under Wyoming law, all occupants must wear safety belts. The driver is responsible for ensuring compliance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is driving more slowly than surrounding traffic generally safe?
options: a:Always safe if the weather is bad.,b:Often a hazard because others may try dangerous passes.,c:Appropriate if you don't know the speed limit.,d:Recommended in all situations.
note: Driving much slower than surrounding traffic can frustrate others and cause unsafe passing maneuvers.

question: Which substances listed can impair driving ability?
options: a:Tranquilizers,b:Only prescription drugs.,c:Only illegal drugs.,d:Only alcohol and marijuana.
note: Many drugs including tranquilizers, sedatives, marijuana, and certain cough or cold medicines can impair driving ability.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Often,b:Never; it confuses other drivers.,c:Whenever it helps prevent a collision.
note: Yielding to avoid a crash is appropriate even if you technically have the right-of-way.

question: When being passed by another vehicle, what is the proper action?
options: a:Move into the passing lane to impede them.,b:Maintain a steady speed to let the other vehicle pass safely.,c:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,d:Brake hard to warn the passing driver.
note: Allow the other vehicle to pass safely by keeping speed and lane steady; do not speed up or brake suddenly.

question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, what is the safest action?
options: a:Speed up.,b:Challenge them.,c:Get out of their way.
note: Avoid engagement—give aggressive drivers space, do not retaliate, and allow them to pass when safe.

question: As daylight fades, which lights should you turn on to help others see you?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:High beams only.,c:Emergency flashers.,d:Low beam headlights.
note: Turn on your low beam headlights as daylight fades so other drivers can see your vehicle without causing glare.

question: What does a red arrow pointing right mean at an intersection?
options: a:You may turn after making a complete stop.,b:You must not turn in that direction until the light changes.,c:You may turn after slowing and checking for traffic.,d:You may turn if no pedestrians are present.
note: A red arrow means 'stop' for that direction; do not turn against a red arrow until it changes.

question: What lane entitlement do motorcycles have?
options: a:Only the bicycle lane.,b:Half the lane width.,c:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.,d:The shoulder only.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the same full lane width as other vehicles; they should be treated as regular traffic participants.

question: Driving while under the influence of medication that impairs you is:
options: a:Allowed if it is over-the-counter.,b:Under no circumstances permitted.,c:Allowed if you don't feel drowsy.,d:Allowed if it was prescribed by a physician.
note: It is illegal and unsafe to drive under the influence of any substance—prescription, over-the-counter, or illegal—that impairs your driving.

question: When driving past parked cars, what precaution should you take?
options: a:Drive closely to the parked vehicles to allow more room for moving traffic.,b:Expect everyone to respect your right-of-way.,c:Be prepared for a person or vehicle to unexpectedly enter your lane.
note: Keep space away from parked cars; people or car doors can suddenly enter your path.

question: How should you drive in fog?
options: a:Turn on and off your lights to alert others.,b:Slow down and use low beam headlights.,c:Slow down and use high beam headlights.,d:Drive at normal speed with hazards on.
note: In fog you should slow down and use your low beams; if visibility is extremely poor, pull off the roadway and wait.

question: Why should you avoid making sudden stops in front of large trucks or buses?
options: a:Large trucks and buses travel at higher speeds than small vehicles.,b:Small vehicle drivers cannot adequately see large trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.,c:Large trucks and buses require longer distances to stop than smaller passenger vehicles.
note: Large vehicles need more distance to stop; sudden stops ahead of them risk rear-end collisions because they may not stop in time.

question: What is the only thing that lowers blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Time,b:Eating foods high in fat.,c:Drinking caffeine
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize and reduce blood alcohol concentration; nothing else speeds this process.

question: Which statement best describes defensive drivers' thinking?
options: a:They know other drivers will do the right thing.,b:They expect no breaks and give none.,c:They consider what other drivers might do and are prepared to react.
note: Defensive drivers anticipate potential mistakes by others and act to reduce risk.

question: How must you respond to a flashing red traffic light at an intersection?
options: a:Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.,b:Yield to traffic and proceed without stopping.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.,d:Come to a complete stop
note: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the effect of continually passing vehicles on a two-lane road?
options: a:It increases your risk of a collision.,b:It helps reduce traffic congestion.,c:It gets you there more quickly and safely.,d:It is always legal if the road is clear.
note: Repeated passing on two-lane roads increases your chances of a collision; avoid unnecessary passing.

question: When should you yield to a pedestrian?
options: a:Only when they wave you on.,b:Only when the traffic signals favor pedestrians.,c:At all times to avoid striking them,d:Only if they are in a marked crosswalk.
note: Always do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, even if the pedestrian is not following laws.

question: When driving on slippery surfaces like snow or ice, what should you do before descending steep hills?
options: a:Use cruise control to maintain speed.,b:Shift to a low gear.,c:Follow other vehicles closely.,d:Make sudden speed changes to maintain control.
note: To help prevent skids on slippery hills, shift to a low gear before the descent and make gradual speed changes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, which action is never permitted?
options: a:Signal before moving over.,b:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.,d:Cross the centerline inside an intersection.
note: You should never change lanes by crossing the centerline while inside an intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach an intersection displaying a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red.,c:Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, then proceed.
note: A flashing red signal is treated like a stop sign: stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady green traffic light at an intersection means:
options: a:Adjust your mirrors.,b:Increase your speed.,c:You may continue through the intersection at a safe and reasonable speed
note: A steady green light permits movement through the intersection but you must yield to vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection.

question: Temporary signs in construction or maintenance work areas are what color?
options: a:Orange background with black writing.,b:Green background with white writing.,c:Yellow background with blue writing.,d:Red background with green writing.
note: Work zone signs are orange with black text or symbols to warn drivers of construction and maintenance.

question: Before driving, from where should you remove snow, frost, and ice?
options: a:Only the windshield and passenger window.,b:Just the windshield.,c:All windows and mirrors.
note: Clear all windows and mirrors so you have full visibility before driving.

question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means you must:
options: a:Do not pass.,b:Traffic light ahead.,c:Reduce your speed.
note: A solid yellow line on your side indicates that passing is prohibited.

question: What message does a red octagonal sign display?
options: a:Do not enter.,b:One-way.,c:Stop.
note: An octagonal red sign always means 'STOP.' You must come to a complete stop at that sign.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you face a green light but pedestrians are in the intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Pedestrians must wait for you to cross.,b:You have the right-of-way over pedestrians.,c:You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.
note: Even on a green signal, yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before stopping at a traffic signal or sign, what should you check?
options: a:Check mirrors for surrounding traffic.,b:Turn off your engine.,c:Set the parking brake.,d:Press hard on the accelerator.
note: Scan mirrors to be aware of traffic behind and around you as you slow for a stop.

question: When must you show proof of insurance to law enforcement?
options: a:Only if you are involved in a collision.,b:Only if you are stopped and cited.,c:Proof is not required to be carried in the vehicle.,d:If you are stopped for a citation or involved in a collision.
note: You must provide evidence of insurance upon request during a traffic stop or after an accident.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection, you must:
options: a:Assume oncoming traffic will yield to you.,b:Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,c:Never yield to oncoming traffic.,d:Proceed if you have a green signal regardless of oncoming vehicles.
note: Left-turning drivers must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering an intersection, what is the correct order to scan?
options: a:Right only.,b:Left,c:Left only.
note: Look left, right, then left again before entering an intersection—the second left check accounts for closer vehicles from that direction.

question: If your vehicle starts to skid, which is the correct braking response?
options: a:Apply steady firm braking.,b:Stay off the brakes.,c:Brake abruptly.,d:Pump the brakes quickly.
note: If you begin to skid, do not use the brakes; braking can make the skid worse. Steer to regain control and slow gradually.

question: Which statement about drugs and driving is true?
options: a:Any prescription drug is safe if you don't feel drowsy.,b:Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.,c:All medications are legal to drive on.,d:Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.
note: Legal prescription and over-the-counter medications can impair driving; it's illegal to drive under the influence of any drug that reduces your ability to drive safely.

question: At night, what is a recommended safety practice?
options: a:Drive at the posted speed regardless of visibility.,b:Always use high beams.,c:Increase your following distance.,d:Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
note: Because visibility is reduced at night, increase following distance so you have more time to react if the car ahead stops suddenly.

question: When is highway pavement especially slippery?
options: a:If it has been raining for one to two hours.,b:When it has just begun to rain.,c:If it has been raining for several hours.,d:Only when ice is present.
note: Shortly after rain begins, oil and debris mix with water creating a slippery surface, making driving hazardous.

question: What must you do at a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights?
options: a:Drive around the gates if you do not see a train.,b:Stop well behind the gates and wait until they are lifted before proceeding.,c:Slow down and proceed cautiously around the gates.,d:Cross quickly before the gates fully lower.
note: You must stop and remain behind lowered gates and flashing lights; it is illegal and dangerous to go around them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes or passing, what should you do?
options: a:Drive with one hand on the wheel.,b:Check mirrors and blind spots,c:Honk to warn others.,d:Increase your speed dramatically.
note: Always check mirrors, look over your shoulder to check blind spots, and signal before changing lanes.

question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn, what may they legally do?
options: a:Use the left lane.,b:Cut through all lanes unpredictably.,c:Use the sidewalk to turn left.,d:Always wait on the side of the road.
note: Bicyclists may use the left lane when making a left turn; expect them to act like other traffic when turning.

question: How do sudden wind gusts on highways affect vehicles?
options: a:Only cause visibility problems.,b:Generally affect only the movement of large vehicles.,c:Can cause problems for all vehicles.
note: Strong winds can affect vehicles of all sizes—reducing stability, moving debris, and lowering visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which describes the best mindset regarding other drivers and right-of-way rules?
options: a:You always have the right-of-way if signs indicate so.,b:Assume most drivers obey right-of-way rules.,c:Assume all drivers follow right-of-way rules.,d:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way.
note: Do not assume others will yield correctly; be prepared to give up your right-of-way to avoid a crash.

question: What color are various traffic control devices used in construction and maintenance areas?
options: a:Green.,b:Red.,c:Orange.,d:Yellow.
note: Work zones use orange signs, cones, and barriers to alert drivers to changed conditions and hazards.

question: What do orange-colored traffic signs indicate?
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Construction and maintenance warnings.,c:General warning signs.
note: Orange signs are used for temporary work zone warnings and alerts about construction or maintenance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to drive on the shoulder to pass another car?
options: a:If traffic is stopped in your lane.,b:If the vehicle ahead is turning left.,c:Under no circumstances.,d:If the shoulder is wide enough.
note: Never pass another vehicle by driving on the shoulder; the other driver will not expect you to be there.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline next to your lane indicate?
options: a:Passing is not permitted.,b:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:Passing on the left is allowed when the way ahead is clear.
