note: A dashed yellow line on your side means you may cross the centerline to pass if no oncoming traffic and it's safe.

question: On an interstate, to avoid vehicles merging from right on-ramps, you should:
options: a:Slow down and stay in the lane.,b:Change lanes to the left when safe.,c:Maintain your speed and position.,d:Block the ramp by speeding up.
note: When traffic allows, move out of the right-hand lane to let vehicles enter from on-ramps; adjust lanes safely and signal.

question: Under heavy fog with low visibility, how should you drive?
options: a:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.,b:Increase your speed so you do not cause an accident.,c:Turn on your high beam headlights.
note: Reduce speed and use low beams in fog; if visibility becomes too poor, pull off the road safely and wait for conditions to improve.

question: What is true about large trucks compared to passenger vehicles?
options: a:They are more maneuverable than cars.,b:They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.,c:They are always equipped to stop more quickly.,d:They stop in the same distance as smaller cars at the same speed.
note: Large trucks require more distance to stop than passenger vehicles traveling at the same speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection, you should:
options: a:Only yield to other vehicles,b:Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,c:Expect oncoming traffic and pedestrians to yield to you.,d:Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: When turning left, yield the right-of-way to oncoming vehicles and to any pedestrians in the crosswalk before completing the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an oncoming vehicle has very bright headlights at night, how should you respond?
options: a:Flash your high beams.,b:Stare directly at the headlights to adjust your vision.,c:Look toward the right edge of your lane.,d:Turn off your headlights.
note: Avoid looking directly at oncoming high beams; glance toward the right edge of the roadway until the vehicle passes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal is green but an officer signals you to stop, what should you do?
options: a:Obey the traffic signal.,b:Do what the vehicle in front of you does.,c:Obey the officer.
note: Drivers must follow directions from police officers or other authorized personnel even if those directions differ from traffic signals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When first approaching a yield sign, what should you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop every time.,b:Increase your speed.,c:Check for cross traffic and be prepared to stop if needed.
note: Assess cross traffic when approaching a yield; stop only if necessary to avoid conflict.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you face a green light but the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Turn left and find another route.,b:Stay out of the intersection until traffic ahead clears.,c:Follow the other vehicles and enter the intersection.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it—blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

question: What should you do to avoid losing traction on wet roads?
options: a:Slow down and avoid abrupt maneuvers.,b:Apply the brakes firmly.,c:Make abrupt turns to keep control.
note: Reduce speed and avoid sudden steering or braking to maintain traction on wet surfaces.

question: Because motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are harder to see, you should:
options: a:Share your lane with them at all times.,b:Make frequent visual checks and slow down if needed.,c:Assume they will yield to you.,d:Always honk when approaching them.
note: Small vehicles are easily missed in blind spots; constantly check for them and be prepared to react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, what must you do to check for nearby vehicles?
options: a:Signal after you start changing lanes.,b:Rely solely on the rearview mirror.,c:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,d:Rely only on the side mirror.
note: Blind spots are not visible in mirrors; always glance over your shoulder before moving laterally.

question: An oncoming vehicle has high beams on at night, making it hard to see. Where should you look?
options: a:Look ahead toward the right edge of your lane.,b:Look straight ahead in your lane.,c:Look ahead toward the left edge of your lane.
note: Avoid staring at the bright lights; glance toward the right edge of your lane and use peripheral vision to monitor the oncoming vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn, you must yield to which vehicles?
options: a:Overtaking cars.,b:Oncoming cars.,c:No one.
note: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming vehicles proceeding straight; only turn when the path is clear and it is safe to do so.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, how should you re-enter the roadway?
options: a:Wait until safe,b:Accelerate and jerk the steering wheel back onto the pavement.,c:Turn back onto the roadway immediately at full speed.,d:Stop and call for assistance immediately.
note: Do not turn back abruptly; reduce speed, check traffic, and ease gradually back onto the pavement when safe.

question: When should you use your horn?
options: a:To warn others to help prevent a collision.,b:To alert a pedestrian who is blind.,c:To greet a friend on the road.,d:To get a slow driver to move over.
note: Use the horn only when necessary to help prevent a collision; do not use it to urge slower drivers or bicyclists to move or to greet people.

question: Where are a truck's blind spots typically located?
options: a:Both on the immediate left of the cab and directly behind the body.,b:Directly behind the body.,c:On the immediate left of the cab.
note: Large trucks have significant blind zones on their left side and directly behind; if you can't see the driver's face in their mirror, they likely can't see you.

question: What color are regulatory traffic signs typically?
options: a:Green.,b:Yellow.,c:White.
note: Regulatory signs (speed limits, stop, yield) are usually white with black, red, or green symbols or text.

question: What are blind spots?
options: a:Areas near the rear corners of your vehicle that cannot be seen in mirrors.,b:Traffic control devices.,c:Spots in your vision when you become fatigued.
note: Blind spots are areas not visible in mirrors—check over your shoulder before changing lanes.

question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane, what must you do?
options: a:Honk to let them know you are there.,b:Speed up to clear the area.,c:Yield the right-of-way to the pedestrian.,d:Require the pedestrian to wait until you pass.
note: Blind or partially blind pedestrians must be given the right-of-way and allowed to cross safely.

question: If you must park where it is not usually used for parking, what should you ensure?
options: a:Only park on the sidewalk if necessary.,b:Park five feet from the curb.,c:Park with your reverse lights on.,d:That your vehicle is visible to drivers approaching from any direction.
note: When parking in unusual areas, make sure your vehicle does not create a hazard and is visible to other drivers.

question: If you must stop on the interstate in an emergency, what should you do?
options: a:Get out and flag down help from passing cars.,b:Pull off the road,c:Leave the vehicle and stand behind it on the shoulder.,d:Sound your horn at passing cars to get assistance.
note: If you must stop on the interstate shoulder, activate your emergency flashers and remain in the vehicle if it is safe to do so due to high-speed traffic.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Leave the wheels straight.,b:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,c:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb if brakes fail.

question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Wait for a green light before proceeding.,d:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
note: A flashing yellow cautions drivers to slow and be alert before crossing the intersection.

question: What should you do if bad weather reduces visibility?
options: a:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.,b:Speed up to get off the road quickly.,c:Increase your following distance.,d:Keep normal following distance but drive slower.
note: When visibility is poor due to weather, increase your following distance to allow more time to react.

question: If you are under 21, driving with what blood alcohol level can lead to license suspension?
options: a:Any amount.,b:0.08 percent or more.,c:0.15 percent or more.
note: Wyoming has a zero-tolerance policy for drivers under 21—any detectable alcohol can result in penalties including license suspension.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out, how should you respond?
options: a:Pull over immediately without slowing.,b:Hold the steering wheel tightly,c:Apply the brake and hold it firmly.
note: Keep control by holding the wheel, easing off the gas, and braking lightly until you can safely move off the road.

question: What is the purpose of work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs?
options: a:To permanently reroute traffic.,b:To make drivers angry about slow traffic.,c:To keep traffic out of hazardous work zones and protect workers.,d:To indicate free parking areas.
note: Work zone devices are used to warn and direct drivers to stay out of dangerous areas and protect road workers.

question: What is a major danger of excessive speed?
options: a:It saves time.,b:It helps you maneuver obstacles.,c:It increases the likelihood of serious injury and death.
note: Excessive speed is a leading cause of crashes and severe injuries and does not reliably save time.

question: What should you avoid doing when driving through a construction zone?
options: a:Passing carefully.,b:Being prepared to slow or stop for workers and equipment.,c:Slowing to look at the scene (rubbernecking).
note: Do not slow to stare at workers or incidents; maintain caution and follow posted directions to keep traffic moving safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs you to go through a red light, what should you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop before proceeding.,b:Stop until the light turns green.,c:Obey the officer and proceed through the intersection.
note: Instructions from a traffic officer override traffic signals—follow their direction.

question: When taking any medicine, what should you do about driving?
options: a:Have someone follow you home.,b:Keep your window open and drive more slowly.,c:Consult your doctor about the effects before driving.
note: Some prescription and over-the-counter drugs can impair driving—check with a doctor or pharmacist about side effects.

question: How should you drive in a construction zone?
options: a:Expect construction workers to yield to motorists.,b:Slightly increase your speed.,c:Expect the unexpected.
note: Drive with extra caution in work zones: slow down, obey posted speeds, and watch for changing conditions or workers.

question: At what speed should you travel relative to conditions and surrounding traffic?
options: a:At the speed of the vehicles surrounding you.,b:At a speed appropriate for the road and weather conditions.,c:At the posted speed limit regardless of conditions.
note: Drive at a speed that is safe for current conditions while obeying posted limits; adjust for weather and traffic.

question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?
options: a:Alcohol affects judgment,b:If you can walk straight after drinking,c:Alcohol only affects driving after several drinks.,d:Being under the legal BAC limit means driving is unimpaired.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, reaction time, and coordination even at low levels, affecting driving safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, you should check mirrors and also:
options: a:Glance over your shoulder to check blind spots.,b:Never look over your right shoulder.,c:Signal only after you begin moving.,d:Always slow down in your lane.
note: In addition to mirror checks, a shoulder glance confirms there is no vehicle in your blind spot.

question: What minimum following distance should you maintain when driving in winter weather?
options: a:One second.,b:Two seconds.,c:Six seconds.,d:Four seconds.
note: In winter conditions you should allow at least a four-second following distance to give yourself extra stopping time.

question: If you expect a rear-end collision, which action should you avoid doing?
options: a:Release your seat belt.,b:Press your head against the head restraint.,c:Brace yourself.
note: Do not release your seat belt; brace yourself against the seat and restraint to reduce injury.

question: When parking on any hill, what should you always do?
options: a:Park with one rear wheel touching the curb.,b:Turn your wheels parallel to the road regardless of curb.,c:Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in 'park' (or in gear).,d:Leave the vehicle in neutral so it can roll if needed.
note: Always set the parking brake and leave the vehicle in park or in gear; position wheels so the vehicle won't roll into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is passing another vehicle permitted?
options: a:When you are on a hill or curve.,b:When an oncoming vehicle is approaching.,c:When there is a solid line next to your lane.,d:When the centerline next to your lane is a broken line.
note: Passing is permitted only where a broken centerline indicates it is safe and legal to do so.

question: Which statement about motorcycles on the road is true?
options: a:Motorcycles have the same rights and responsibilities as larger motor vehicles.,b:Motorcycles always must yield to cars.,c:Motorcycles are exempt from traffic rules.,d:Motorcycles must use sidewalks when possible.
note: Motorcycles are vehicles under the law and must be given the same respect and space as other vehicles.

question: When driving in fog, which headlights are best to use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:Four-way flashers only.,c:High beam headlights.,d:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow; high beams can reflect and reduce visibility.

question: When passing another vehicle, how should you complete the maneuver?
options: a:Pass the vehicle as slowly as possible.,b:Pass the vehicle as safely and as quickly as possible.,c:Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.
note: Pass promptly and safely, and return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

question: When should you allow an extra cushion of space behind the vehicle ahead?
options: a:When following a station wagon.,b:When following a small passenger car.,c:When following a driver who may not be able to see the rear of their vehicle
note: Increase following distance behind large vehicles because they may have limited rear visibility and can block your view.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who should yield when you are entering interstate traffic from an entrance or acceleration ramp?
options: a:You should yield to drivers already on the interstate.,b:Drivers on the interstate must yield to you.,c:You always have the right-of-way.,d:No one should yield; merge by force.
note: Vehicles merging onto the interstate must yield to the traffic already traveling on it and merge safely into gaps.

question: Which road surface is most likely to freeze first?
options: a:A shaded residential street.,b:A bridge or overpass.,c:A tunnel.,d:An intersection.
note: Bridges and overpasses are exposed on all sides and can freeze before adjacent road surfaces.

question: After snow or rain on cold days, which area of road is most likely to be icy?
options: a:A hilly,b:A residential road.,c:A shaded area of the roadway.
note: Shaded sections freeze sooner and thaw later, so they are more likely to be icy.

question: After a minor intersection collision with no injuries, what should you do if it is safe?
options: a:Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until law enforcement arrives.,b:Not move your vehicle for any reason.,c:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane
note: If no one is injured and you can safely do so, move vehicles out of traffic lanes to prevent further collisions and restore flow.

question: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights, you should:
options: a:Flash your high beams.,b:Stay focused on the centerline on the road.,c:Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
note: Glance briefly toward the right edge of your lane to avoid being blinded by oncoming headlights while maintaining awareness of the vehicle.

question: On the highway, regularly scanning well ahead of your vehicle:
options: a:Reduces the need for last-minute braking or turning.,b:Allows you to spot upcoming police officers.,c:Helps you keep up with traffic.,d:Has no effect on fuel consumption.
note: Watching far ahead and being prepared reduces the need for sudden braking or turning, helps traffic flow, and can save fuel.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a two-lane road, what should you judge carefully?
options: a:How loudly to honk as you pass.,b:The number of passengers in the other vehicle.,c:The color of the other driver’s vehicle.,d:The distance and speed of any oncoming vehicles.
note: Be certain there is enough clear distance ahead to pass safely by judging oncoming vehicle speed and distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Within a curve if you do not see oncoming traffic.,b:Within an intersection even if no oncoming vehicles are present.,c:Where signs and/or pavement markings permit passing and it is safe to do so.
note: Only pass where pavement markings and signs allow and you have clear sight and sufficient space.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway, what distance should you maintain?
options: a:No more than one car length to be visible in their mirrors.,b:Follow closely because the truck driver can see farther ahead.,c:Directly beside the truck to avoid blind spots.,d:Stay farther behind than you would for a passenger vehicle.
note: Maintain extra following distance behind trucks because they block your view and need more stopping distance.

question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, how should you drive?
options: a:Drive slowly enough to stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.,b:Keep the instrument panel lights bright to be seen by others.,c:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic for visibility.,d:Use high beams continuously to see farther.
note: On dimly lit streets drive at a speed that allows you to stop within the distance your headlights illuminate.

question: A pedestrian with a guide dog is at the corner ready to cross before you make a right turn—what should you do?
options: a:Wait until the person crosses the street before making your turn.,b:Turn off your engine until they cross.,c:Tell the pedestrian when to cross.
note: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes must be given the right-of-way; wait until they finish crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as vehicles on your right and left, you should:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your right.,b:Proceed first because you are in the center.,c:Wait until the intersection is completely empty before proceeding.,d:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your left.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where vehicles arrive simultaneously, yield to the vehicle on your right and proceed in the order vehicles arrived.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb, which direction do you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn them to the right toward the side of the road.,b:Turn them straight ahead.,c:Turn them left toward the center of the road.,d:Turn them toward oncoming traffic.
note: When parking downhill on a road with or without a curb, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road so the vehicle rolls away from traffic if brakes fail.

question: When driving in snowy or icy conditions, what should you avoid using?
options: a:Cruise control.,b:A low gear going down hills.,c:Gradual steering inputs.,d:Gentle braking.
note: Do not use cruise control on snow or ice because it can cause loss of control if tires lose traction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing, when should you return to the right lane?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.,c:When you are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: Return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your mirror to ensure safe spacing.

question: On a slippery road, how should your following distance change?
options: a:Keep it the same as normal.,b:Decrease it to stay closer for better traction.,c:Increase it so you are farther from the car ahead than normal.,d:Only increase distance if driving over 50 mph.
note: You need more stopping distance on slippery roads, so increase the following distance compared to dry conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before entering a curve?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Activate your turn signal.,c:Increase your speed.,d:Brake hard in the curve.
note: Slow down before entering curves when conditions require; do not exceed the posted speed limit.

question: When backing up, what technique should you use?
options: a:Look directly through the rear window while backing slowly.,b:Rely solely on your mirrors.,c:Accelerate to clear the area quickly.,d:Only use a backup camera if available.
note: When reversing, turn and look through the rear window rather than relying only on mirrors; proceed slowly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:Never for pedestrians.,b:Only at stop signs.,c:At any intersection where a police officer orders you to stop and at a red traffic light.,d:Only when another vehicle signals you to stop.
note: You must obey directions from officers directing traffic and must stop at red lights; both require stopping your vehicle.

question: Why should you avoid using high beam headlights when driving in fog or mist?
options: a:High beams will damage your headlights faster.,b:High beams are illegal in foggy conditions.,c:High beams create glare by reflecting back into your eyes.,d:High beams make your tail lights less visible.
note: In fog or mist, high beams reflect off moisture and can shine back into your eyes, reducing visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic from an alley or driveway and crossing a sidewalk, you should:
options: a:Expect pedestrians to yield to you.,b:Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.,c:Sound your horn and proceed if the sidewalk looks clear.,d:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.
note: When leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot, you must stop before driving onto the sidewalk area; pedestrians and roadway traffic have the right-of-way.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway, how should you position your vehicle?
options: a:Closer behind the truck than you would if following a passenger vehicle.,b:Farther behind the truck than you would a passenger vehicle.,c:To the right side of the truck and wait to pass.
note: Maintain a greater following distance behind large trucks because they have longer stopping distances and large blind spots.

question: When following a motorcycle, why should you leave extra space in front of your vehicle?
options: a:Because station wagons need extra space.,b:Because passenger vehicles require more following distance.,c:Because motorcycles can stop more quickly and are harder to see
note: Motorcycles can stop quickly and may be difficult to see; allow more space to react safely if they brake or fall.

question: Which of the following will reduce your blood alcohol content (BAC) and its effects?
options: a:Drinking coffee or caffeine.,b:Exercising vigorously.,c:Time.,d:Eating fatty foods.
note: Only the passage of time removes alcohol and its impairing effects from the body.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you approach a roundabout, what action should you take?
options: a:Maintain your speed.,b:Increase your speed.,c:Decrease your speed and prepare to enter.
note: Slow down when approaching a roundabout; these are designed for low-speed operation.

question: When are rumble strips used and why?
options: a:They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.,b:They signal a need to change lanes immediately.,c:They alert inattentive drivers that their vehicle has left the travel lane through noise and vibration.,d:They are decorative roadway features.
note: Rumble strips create vibration and sound to warn drowsy or inattentive drivers they are leaving the travel lane or approaching a hazard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit in residential areas?
options: a:45 mph.,b:20 mph.,c:30 mph.
note: The standard speed limit in residential areas is 30 mph unless a different limit is posted.

question: If you are angry after an argument, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Loudly play the radio while driving.,b:Take a few minutes to cool off before driving.,c:Drive on the interstate to let off steam.
note: Emotional impairment affects judgment—calm down and regain focus before getting behind the wheel.

question: A vehicle ahead stops at a crosswalk. How should you respond?
options: a:Cautiously pass the stopped vehicle at 10 mph or less.,b:Honk so the stopped driver will move.,c:Stop and proceed only after all pedestrians have cleared the crossing.,d:Change lanes and pass the vehicle quickly.
note: You must not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk because pedestrians may be crossing; wait until all pedestrians have crossed.

question: Which is a dangerous habit when driving through work zones?
options: a:Tailgating and failing to watch for workers and equipment.,b:Slowing to the posted work zone speed.,c:Using the far lane when directed to merge.,d:Following all posted signs and directions.
note: Following too closely and ignoring workers or equipment are hazardous behaviors in work zones.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on the left, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.,b:When you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:After about three seconds.
note: Move back only when you can clearly see the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, ensuring safe clearance.

question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?
options: a:They do not follow the same rules as motor vehicles.,b:Because a motorcycle can stop much faster than standard vehicles.,c:They brake more slowly than motor vehicles.
note: Motorcycles can stop quickly and are harder to see—leave extra space to avoid a rear-end collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto the freeway, what speed should you aim to be driving?
options: a:The posted speed limit for surface streets.,b:At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.,c:Five to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.,d:Stopped at the end of the ramp to wait for an opening.
note: When merging you should accelerate to match the speed of freeway traffic to enter safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit on Wyoming secondary highways?
options: a:70 mph.,b:60 mph.,c:55 mph.
note: The statewide speed limit on secondary highways is 70 mph unless a different posted limit applies.

question: After a train passes and you have stopped at the crossing, what should you check before proceeding?
options: a:That signal lights stopped flashing and that no second train is approaching.,b:That the gates remain down before going around them.,c:That the crossing tracks are clear of debris only.,d:That no vehicles are waiting behind you.
note: Even after a train passes, look for a second train and do not go until gates are up and warning lights have stopped flashing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you respond to a flashing yellow light at an intersection?
options: a:Stop before crossing the intersection.,b:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.,c:Wait for the green light before proceeding.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution—slow down and be alert to other traffic and pedestrians.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
options: a:Only peripheral vision.,b:None if taken in small amounts.,c:Alertness,d:Only the ability to steer straight.
note: Alcohol and many drugs impair alertness, concentration, reaction time, and coordination, affecting driving ability.

question: When a school bus is loading or unloading children, drivers must:
options: a:Stop,b:Stop only if driving in the same direction as the bus.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.
note: When a bus displays flashing red lights and its stop arm is extended, all drivers in both directions must stop until it is safe to proceed.

question: What is a likely result of tailgating (following too closely)?
options: a:It reduces collisions by preventing being cut off.,b:It cannot result in a traffic citation.,c:It can frustrate other drivers and may lead to aggressive behavior or citations.
note: Tailgating is unsafe, can provoke others, and may result in traffic penalties—maintain safe following distance.

question: If visibility is reduced to less than 100 feet by weather, what should you do?
options: a:Increase your speed to clear the area quickly.,b:Pull off the road and wait until visibility improves.,c:Drive normally.
note: When you cannot see more than about 100 feet, you cannot safely drive—pull off the road until it clears.

question: A yellow left-turn arrow changing to yellow indicates what?
options: a:Drivers should prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.,b:The protected left turn is about to end.,c:Both of the above.
note: A yellow arrow warns that the protected left-turn phase is ending and drivers should prepare to yield to oncoming traffic when it changes.

question: Which of the following is a safe driving technique?
options: a:Staring at the road ahead of your vehicle.,b:Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.,c:Using your high beam lights in the fog.
note: Scan the road and check your mirrors every few seconds to stay aware of traffic around you; do not stare fixedly ahead.

question: What is usually the first ability affected by alcohol?
options: a:Balance.,b:Judgment.,c:Vision.,d:Coordination.
note: Alcohol first impairs judgment and decision-making, then affects other skills such as vision, coordination, and reaction time.

question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change with speed?
options: a:Are not affected by vehicle speed.,b:Decrease as vehicle speed increases.,c:Increase as vehicle speed increases.
note: Higher speeds lengthen stopping distances and increase the severity of collisions.

question: Which action helps reduce road rage?
options: a:Speed up to pass an aggressive driver.,b:Talk on your cell phone while driving.,c:Always signal when changing lanes.,d:Use your horn frequently.
note: To help prevent road rage, obey laws, signs, and signals and always signal your intentions when changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit in business areas?
options: a:30 mph.,b:20 mph.,c:45 mph.
note: The standard speed limit in business districts is 30 mph unless a different limit is posted.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection controlled by a flashing red signal, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop,b:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red.,c:Reduce your speed and proceed without stopping.
note: Treat a flashing red light like a stop sign: stop fully, yield, and proceed when safe.

question: When you approach a railroad crossing with flashing red lights, what should you do?
options: a:Honk to warn the train.,b:Look for a way around any lowered gates.,c:Come to a complete stop and obey the crossing signals.,d:Drive faster than the train to beat it across.
note: Obey all railroad crossing lights and warnings; never try to go around lowered gates and always stop if signals indicate a train.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a 'Yield' sign, what is required of you?
options: a:Yield only to vehicles on your right.,b:Always slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:Yield the right-of-way to crossing or merging traffic that is close enough to cause conflict.
note: Slow and yield as necessary to any traffic or pedestrians that could cause a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which lane must you use before making a left turn from a one-way street?
options: a:The lane nearest the center of the street.,b:The lane nearest the left curb.,c:Any lane as long as you signal.,d:The lane nearest the right curb.
note: When turning, use the lane closest to the direction you intend to go; for a left turn from a one-way street use the lane nearest the left curb.

question: If you are about to be hit from the rear, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Applying your brakes.,b:Pressing your head firmly against the head restraint.,c:Letting go of the steering wheel.
note: Do not release the wheel; brace yourself, hold the wheel, and press your head against the restraint to reduce whiplash.

question: What is the only proven method for reducing alcohol/drug levels in your system?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Breathe in some fresh air.,c:Give your body time.
note: The only medically proven way to lower blood alcohol concentration is to allow time for metabolism.

question: When a vehicle cuts in front of you creating a hazard, what should you do first?
options: a:Flash your headlights rapidly.,b:Take your foot off the gas to create space.,c:Honk and slam on the brakes.,d:Swerve into the adjacent lane immediately.
note: If a vehicle merges too closely in front of you, easing off the accelerator creates space without abrupt braking or swerving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Should you always drive more slowly than other traffic?
options: a:Only when there is construction ahead.,b:Yes — it is always safer to go slower than surrounding traffic.,c:No — driving too slowly can block traffic and be unsafe.,d:Yes — driving slower is a defensive driving requirement.
note: Driving significantly slower than surrounding traffic can impede traffic flow and increase crash risk; match the flow when safe and legal.

question: What is the best action if you become tired while driving?
options: a:Stop to rest or change drivers.,b:Open a window and continue driving.,c:Drink coffee and continue driving.,d:Play loud music to stay alert.
note: Fatigue reduces reaction time and alertness; pulling over to rest or switching drivers is the safest option.

question: When you are behind a motorcycle and plan to pass, what must you do?
options: a:Never force the rider off the road by honking or crowding.,b:Stay in the right lane because the motorcycle doesn't use the whole lane.,c:Be entirely in the left lane before and during the pass.
note: Give motorcycles a full lane; move fully into the left lane to pass and avoid crowding the motorcycle.

question: How should drivers behave when entering a roundabout?
options: a:Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.,b:Stop before entering every time.,c:Enter quickly to assert right-of-way.,d:Drive in a clockwise direction.
note: Drivers entering a roundabout must yield to traffic already circulating and follow the counterclockwise flow.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out, how should you use the brakes?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly.,c:Use the brakes lightly while holding the steering wheel firmly.
note: Hold the wheel, ease off the gas, and brake gently to slow before pulling off safely.

question: Slowing down just to look at a crash or unusual event usually causes what?
options: a:Improves traffic flow by preventing collisions.,b:Prevents rear-end collisions.,c:Causes traffic congestion.
note: Avoid 'rubbernecking'—slowing to look at incidents causes backups and can lead to secondary collisions.

question: When may you legally go around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate?
options: a:When you can see clearly in both directions.,b:Never.,c:When the warning lights are not flashing.
note: Do not go around or under a lowered railroad gate under any circumstances; wait until it is fully raised and clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are stopped at a red light but a green arrow points your way, when may you go?
options: a:First come to a complete stop.,b:Wait until the light changes.,c:You may go if you are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.
note: A green arrow allows movement in the arrow's direction if you are in the correct lane; yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection first.

question: When should you increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead?
options: a:Are following a small passenger vehicle.,b:Are driving more slowly than the posted speed limit.,c:Are being tailgated by another driver.
note: If you are being tailgated, create extra space in front of you—slow gradually or change lanes—to reduce collision risk.

question: During bad weather, what steering and braking technique is recommended?
options: a:Brake sharply to reduce speed quickly.,b:Steer off the road immediately.,c:Steer and brake smoothly.,d:Turn into a side road and stop on the shoulder.
note: In adverse weather, avoid sudden steering or hard braking; smooth inputs help maintain control.

question: How do stopping distances and collision severity change with speed?
options: a:Both stopping distance and severity increase as vehicle speed increases.,b:Stopping distance decreases as speed increases.,c:Speed has no effect on collision severity.,d:Stopping distance remains constant regardless of speed.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distance and the force of impacts, raising the risk of serious injury.

question: How should you adjust driving on gravel or dirt roads?
options: a:Drive at the same speed as on pavement.,b:Slow down because tires have less traction than on pavement.,c:Use cruise control for steady speed.,d:Expect better traction than on asphalt.
note: Loose surfaces reduce traction and increase stopping distances; slow down and drive cautiously on gravel or dirt roads.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you enter a roundabout, what must you do?
options: a:Both of the above.,b:Yield to any crossing pedestrians and bicyclists.,c:Yield to any car already within the roundabout.
note: When entering a roundabout you must yield to traffic already in the circle and to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing the entrance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing red traffic light require you to do?
options: a:The same as a yield sign.,b:The same as a stop sign; come to a complete stop and yield.,c:The light is about to turn green.
note: A flashing red signal requires a full stop and yielding to others before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In traffic moving at 50–55 mph, you are least likely to have an accident if you:
options: a:Drive much slower than other vehicles.,b:Stay within that speed range (travel with the flow of traffic).,c:Continuously change lanes to find gaps.,d:Drive several miles per hour faster than most other vehicles.
note: Matching the speed of surrounding traffic, within legal limits, reduces speed differentials that cause crashes.

question: How should you change lanes for best safety?
options: a:Gradually and carefully.,b:Without signaling in heavy traffic.,c:When a car is in your blind spot.,d:Quickly and often.
note: Change lanes gradually, check mirrors and blind spots, and signal to minimize collision risk.

question: If the rear of your vehicle begins to skid left, how should you steer?
options: a:Turn your steering wheel left (in the direction of the skid).,b:Turn the wheel sharply to the right immediately.,c:Not turn the steering wheel at all.,d:Brake hard and hold the wheel straight.
note: On a skid, ease off the accelerator and steer in the direction the rear is sliding to regain control.

question: What does a steady red arrow signal mean?
options: a:Proceed with caution in the indicated direction.,b:Drivers may turn in the indicated direction without stopping.,c:Drivers cannot turn in the indicated direction.,d:Drivers may turn after coming to a complete stop.
note: A steady red arrow means traffic in the indicated lane may not proceed in that direction; wait for a green signal to turn or go.

question: How should you respond when you see a person crossing with a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Carefully drive around them.,b:Stop and remain stopped until the person is well away from your path.,c:Wave them across quickly.,d:Honk to let them know you are there.
note: Always yield the right-of-way to blind pedestrians using a cane or guide dog and stop until they are safely past your path.

question: What is the purpose of broken yellow lines on the pavement?
options: a:They indicate no passing zones.,b:They separate lanes moving in the same direction.,c:They separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions and indicate passing may be allowed.
note: Dashed yellow lines separate opposing traffic and mean passing is permitted when safe.

question: When driving in fog you should use which beams?
options: a:Use your high beam headlights.,b:Use your parking lights.,c:Use your low beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog; high beams can reflect off fog and reduce visibility.

question: What does a single broken white line between lanes on a highway allow you to do?
options: a:You cannot cross the line to pass.,b:You may cross the dashed white line to pass or change lanes if safe.,c:You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; you may change lanes or pass where safe.

question: Interstate driving requires drivers to:
options: a:Be constantly alert.,b:Both of the above.,c:Have the ability to safely drive at increased speeds.,d:None of the above.
note: Driving on interstates demands that drivers be alert and able to operate safely at higher speeds.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches from behind or ahead?
options: a:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane.,b:Move into the left lane and drive slowly.,c:Pull over to the right curb or edge of the road and stop.,d:Speed up to avoid it.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights you must pull over to the right edge of the roadway and stop until it passes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, how can you tell you have enough space to return to your lane?
options: a:When you can see both of the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:If the other driver signals for you to re-enter the lane.,c:If you look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.
note: Return to the lane only when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your mirror, indicating safe clearance.

question: What is an important step to take before turning?
options: a:Check traffic in all directions.,b:Always move to the left lane.,c:Increase your speed.
note: Before turning, check rear and side traffic as well as oncoming traffic so you can complete the turn safely.

question: If you plan to pass a pedestrian and an oncoming vehicle is approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Honk for the pedestrian to move over.,b:Keep your speed; the oncoming vehicle must stop.,c:Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first.,d:Quickly swerve into the shoulder to pass both.
note: Handle one hazard at a time: let the oncoming vehicle pass, then pass the pedestrian only if it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the default speed limit in school zones unless otherwise posted?
options: a:20 mph.,b:30 mph.,c:45 mph.
note: Unless a different speed is posted, the speed limit in school zones is 20 miles per hour. Drive cautiously near children.

question: When parking next to a curb, when should you signal?
options: a:Only when pulling next to the curb.,b:Never signal for curb parking.,c:Only when pulling away from the curb.,d:Both when pulling next to the curb and when pulling away from it.
note: Drivers should signal both when pulling up next to a curb and when pulling away to inform other road users of their intention.

question: Any amount of alcohol in the bloodstream may affect a driver's:
options: a:Seatbelt effectiveness.,b:Judgment and physical coordination.,c:Knowledge about road signs.,d:Right-of-way privileges.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol can impair judgment and coordination necessary for safe driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a broken yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:You must stay in your lane at all times.,b:No passing allowed in either direction.,c:A construction zone is ahead.,d:Passing is permitted for traffic on both sides when safe.
note: Broken yellow lines between two-way traffic mean drivers on either side may pass when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you move back into your original lane after passing another vehicle?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:When you have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.,c:When you are 50 feet in front of the passed vehicle.
note: Return to your lane only when you can clearly see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

question: If your vehicle's suspension is failing, what problem can result?
options: a:Squealing brakes.,b:Slack in the steering.,c:Vehicle control problems.
note: A faulty suspension reduces vehicle control and stability, especially over bumps and uneven surfaces.

question: What can continuous hard braking on snow and ice cause?
options: a:Keeping the brakes from freezing.,b:Locking of the front wheels and loss of steering control.,c:Helping you stop faster.
note: Continuous hard braking on icy roads can lock wheels and cause loss of steering—avoid sudden hard braking.

question: You see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you on a city street. What should you do?
options: a:Drive to the right edge of the road and slow down.,b:Stay in your lane,c:Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles by pulling to the right edge of the road and stopping until the vehicle has passed; if in an intersection, clear it first.

question: If heavy smoke covers the road ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on four-way flashers and continue at the same speed.,b:Accelerate through the smoke to clear it quickly.,c:Turn on high beams and continue cautiously.,d:Reduce speed
note: If smoke obstructs vision, slow down, exit the roadway to a safe place, and assess the situation before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what circumstances may you legally block an intersection?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:If you are yielding to pedestrians.,c:Only if you entered on a green light.,d:During rush hour only.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless you can clear it; blocking an intersection is illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are being passed in a no-passing zone, what should you do?
options: a:Pull completely off the road.,b:Accelerate to prevent them from passing.,c:Maintain your speed and position to let the other driver re-enter safely.,d:Slam on your brakes to warn them.
note: If another vehicle illegally passes you, stay steady to allow the passing driver to safely return to the lane when possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching a steady yellow traffic signal and you have not entered the intersection—what should you do?
options: a:Come to a safe stop.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed through the intersection.,c:Speed up to beat the red light.
note: A steady yellow warns the light will change to red; if you haven't entered, slow and stop safely.

question: A five-sided (pentagon) sign on the roadway indicates:
options: a:Stop sign.,b:Regulatory sign.,c:School zone or school crossing sign.
note: Pentagon-shaped signs are used to warn drivers of a school zone or school crossing ahead.

question: If the roadway is wet or icy, you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Speed up.,c:Drive at the posted speed.
note: Wet or icy conditions reduce tire traction; slow down and increase following distance to maintain control.

question: If pedestrians are illegally crossing mid-block, how must you respond?
options: a:You may proceed without stopping.,b:You must stop for them.,c:Drive slowly past them without stopping.,d:Honk to make them move out of the way.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians at all times; even if they are not in a crosswalk, you must stop for them.

question: If your car becomes disabled on the highway, where should you park if possible?
options: a:With all four wheels off the traveled portion of the highway.,b:Stop in the right lane.,c:In the center median.,d:Partially on the roadway.
note: If possible, move your vehicle completely off the main traveled portion of the road and turn on hazard lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive slower than the flow of traffic, what is likely to happen?
options: a:You will always improve traffic flow.,b:You will demonstrate defensive driving.,c:You will interfere with traffic and could be cited.,d:You will reduce the chance of collisions.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow can block the movement of traffic and may lead to a citation.

question: If you see a deep puddle on the roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Maintain the posted speed to make it through the water.,b:Shift into neutral as you drive through the water.,c:Avoid the puddle if possible.
note: Avoid large puddles when possible to reduce the risk of hydroplaning and damage to your vehicle.

question: Which factor affects how quickly a person absorbs alcohol?
options: a:Intelligence.,b:Height.,c:Body weight.
note: Absorption is affected by weight, biological sex, food in the stomach, and amount consumed.

question: When you approach a stopped school bus on the opposite side of a divided highway, you should:
options: a:Must stop until the bus begins moving.,b:Must stop until the stop arm is lowered.,c:Stop only if children are visible crossing the road.,d:May continue driving.
note: If the highway is divided by a physical barrier or median, drivers on the opposite side may continue; otherwise both directions must stop for a bus with flashing red lights.

question: What type of information is provided by blue traffic signs?
options: a:Mileage distances to locations.,b:Construction and maintenance.,c:Motorist services such as rest areas
note: Blue signs indicate services and facilities available to motorists like hospitals and rest areas.

question: If your vehicle develops a mechanical problem on the roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Signal and pull into the slow lane.,b:Stop in your lane and put on your hazard lights.,c:Turn on your hazard lights and pull completely off the road.
note: If possible, get off the roadway, away from traffic, and activate emergency flashers so other drivers know you have trouble.

question: Which medications may affect your ability to drive safely?
options: a:Any medication.,b:Only illegal drugs.,c:Only sleeping pills.,d:Only over-the-counter cold remedies.
note: Any medication—prescription or over-the-counter—can impair driving. When starting a new drug, do not drive until you know how it affects you.

question: What do double solid yellow lane markings indicate?
options: a:The lane to the right may pass.,b:No passing allowed from either direction.,c:Both lanes may pass.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and prohibit passing from both directions.

question: Drowsiness while driving can have what effect, similar to alcohol and drugs?
options: a:Make you feel better.,b:Impair your judgment.,c:Help you to be a better driver.
note: Lack of sleep slows reaction time and impairs judgment and awareness, much like alcohol and drugs.

question: What should you do when approaching a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way and allow them to cross safely.,b:Honk to let them know to clear the way.,c:Swerve quickly around them.,d:Ask them to wait on the curb.
note: Blind pedestrians using a cane or guide dog must be given the right-of-way and allowed to cross safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection tells drivers to:
options: a:Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.,b:Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down, be alert, and proceed with caution—no full stop is required unless directed.

question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
options: a:Whenever you need to use them.,b:Before you start driving.,c:Before you get into the car.
note: Adjust mirrors before moving the vehicle—also adjust your seat and fasten your safety belt as part of a pre-drive routine.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach a steady yellow light and have not entered the intersection, you should:
options: a:Come to a safe stop.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.,c:Speed up to beat the red light.
note: A steady yellow warns the signal is about to turn red; stop safely if you have not yet entered the intersection.

question: How is distracted driving defined?
options: a:Anything that takes attention away from driving.,b:Anything that causes you to focus more on driving.,c:Anything that forces you to take evasive action.,d:Driving while listening to the radio.
note: Distracted driving includes any activity that diverts eyes, hands, or mind from driving tasks and is a leading cause of crashes.

question: What do yellow center lines on the road separate?
options: a:Parking areas from driving lanes.,b:Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.,c:Carpool lanes from regular lanes.,d:Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
note: Yellow lines mark the center of a two-way road and separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On the freeway, how should you react when traffic is merging into your lane?
options: a:Always maintain your exact position regardless.,b:Signal the merging driver to stop.,c:Make room for merging traffic when it is safe to do so.,d:Assert your right-of-way by speeding up.
note: When safe, adjust speed or change lanes to allow merging vehicles to enter smoothly.

question: How does a BAC of 0.02 percent affect driving risk?
options: a:It has no effect on your driving.,b:It won't put other drivers at risk.,c:It nearly doubles the chance of having an accident.
note: Even low BAC levels significantly increase crash risk; each small increase raises the likelihood of a serious crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Into any lane available.,b:Into the first (leftmost) lane of the one-way street.,c:Into the parking lane if necessary.,d:Into the second lane from the left.
note: When turning onto a one-way street, turn into the lane closest to the curb and the direction of travel (the first available lane).

question: What does a broken yellow line between opposing lanes mean?
options: a:Passing is permitted when it is safe to do so.,b:Both lanes are moving in the same direction.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: A dashed (broken) yellow line separates opposite directions and indicates passing is allowed when safe.

question: If the roadway ahead is flooded, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed if other cars are going through.,b:Do not drive through the flooded area; turn around and find another route.,c:Drive only in the center of the road to avoid hazards.,d:Slam on the brakes and stop immediately in the water.
note: Never attempt to drive through floodwater; even shallow water can hide hazards or sweep vehicles away.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can you check your blind spot when changing lanes?
options: a:Trust your vehicle's sensors exclusively.,b:Use only the side mirror.,c:Use only the inside rearview mirror.,d:Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
note: Physically looking over your shoulder reveals areas not visible in mirrors and helps ensure a safe lane change.

question: Why should you leave extra space in front of a large truck?
options: a:Trucks need more distance to stop than cars.,b:It improves your fuel efficiency.,c:Trucks will always signal for you to merge.,d:So other drivers can pass the truck easily.
note: Large trucks require longer stopping distances than passenger vehicles; do not cut in front of them and then slow down.

question: If weather or light conditions require lights, which should you use?
options: a:Interior lights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:High beams.,d:Parking lights.
note: Use low beam headlights when conditions require lights; high beams can reflect and worsen visibility in adverse conditions.

question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, you should:
options: a:Look directly at the oncoming headlights.,b:Turn your lights on and off.,c:Switch your lights to high beam.,d:Glance toward the right edge of the road.
note: If an oncoming vehicle's lights are blinding, look toward the right edge of the road and follow it by using the painted edge lines until you pass the vehicle.

question: Which lights should you use to improve visibility in rain or fog?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: Use low beams in rain or fog; high beams reduce visibility by reflecting off the weather.

question: If there are oncoming vehicles to your left and parked vehicles to your right, where should you steer?
options: a:All the way onto the shoulder to avoid both.,b:Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.,c:Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.,d:A middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
note: Keep a middle course to give safe clearance from both oncoming traffic and parked vehicles.

question: When parallel parked facing downhill, which way should you turn the wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels away from the side of the road.,b:Keep your wheels straight.,c:Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road.
note: When parking downhill, turn the front wheels toward the curb or edge of the road so the vehicle will roll off the roadway if the brakes fail.

question: An orange and red triangular emblem on the back of a vehicle indicates what?
options: a:Shoulder work ahead.,b:Slow-moving vehicle.,c:The vehicle has the right-of-way.
note: An orange-red triangle signals that a vehicle travels at 25 mph or less (e.g., farm equipment) and other drivers should use caution.

question: How can you reduce the chance of hydroplaning in heavy rain?
options: a:Decrease your speed.,b:Increase speed slightly to cut through water.,c:Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.,d:Move to the shoulder immediately.
note: Lowering your speed in rainy conditions reduces the risk of tires riding on a film of water (hydroplaning).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to exit an interstate, when should you begin to slow down?
options: a:As you approach the deceleration lane.,b:About halfway through the deceleration lane.,c:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.
note: Maintain highway speed until you enter the deceleration lane, then reduce speed to the posted advisory or ramp speed.

question: In fog, rain, or snow, which headlights should you use?
options: a:Fog lights only.,b:High beams.,c:Low beams.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, and snow—high beams can reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:You can cross if gates are down but no train is visible.,b:You have the right-of-way at all railroad crossings.,c:You should use cruise control to maintain speed crossing tracks.,d:You must stop when directed by a flagger
note: Obey all instructions and signals at railroad crossings; stop when directed by signs, lights, or flaggers.

question: How might a large truck behave when turning right onto a multi-lane street?
options: a:It may swing wide to complete the right turn.,b:It may complete its turn in either of the two lanes intentionally.,c:It will always use the left lane to turn right.,d:It must stay entirely in the right lane at all times.
note: Large trucks often need to swing wide when turning because their rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels.

question: When a school bus is stopped with lights flashing and the stop arm extended, what must drivers do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop until all children have left the bus.,b:Change lanes and pass the bus slowly.,c:Stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.
note: When a school bus displays flashing red lights and the stop arm is out, all traffic must stop until it is retracted.

question: A driver's license is considered which of the following?
options: a:Requirement.,b:Right.,c:Privilege.
note: Driving is a privilege granted by the state, not an absolute right; it may be suspended or revoked for violations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when merging onto an interstate highway?
options: a:Select a safe gap and merge into the flow of traffic at freeway speed.,b:Merge across two lanes at once to get over quickly.,c:Always stop at the end of the ramp before entering.,d:Enter at a crawl until you find an opening.
note: When merging, find a gap large enough to safely enter the flow and match the speed of freeway traffic if possible.

question: In heavy fog you should slow down and:
options: a:Turn on your emergency flashers only.,b:Use your low beam headlights.,c:Drive with no lights to avoid glare.,d:Use your high beam headlights.
note: Use low beams (and fog lights if equipped) in fog, rain, or snow; high beams cause glare by reflecting off moisture.

question: When must you obey school crossing guards?
options: a:Only during school hours.,b:At all times.,c:Only if children are present.
note: Drivers must always obey crossing guards' instructions when they are performing their duties near schools.

question: How should you drive when beside a large commercial vehicle?
options: a:Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.,b:Speed up to pass as quickly as possible.,c:Follow closely to reduce wind drag.,d:Avoid driving beside it for long periods because of blind spots.
note: Large commercial vehicles have large blind spots on each side; avoid driving beside them for long stretches.

question: How should you respond to a flashing yellow traffic light at an intersection?
options: a:Wait for a green light.,b:Slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution.,c:Stop before entering the intersection.,d:Yield to all traffic before crossing
note: A flashing yellow means you should reduce speed and cross the intersection carefully after checking for hazards.

question: What is the correct approach when driving in work zones?
options: a:Follow the driver in front of you closely.,b:Pass the driver in front as soon as possible.,c:Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.,d:Ignore temporary speed limits.
note: In work zones increase your following distance and avoid tailgating to protect workers and other drivers.

question: How does increasing blood alcohol concentration (BAC) affect you?
options: a:Your coordination improves.,b:You become more intoxicated and impaired.,c:Your reaction time decreases slightly but judgment improves.,d:You become more sober.
note: Higher BAC means greater impairment of judgment, coordination, and reaction time.

question: If you feel fatigued while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Open all windows and keep going.,b:Increase your speed to finish driving sooner.,c:Turn up the radio and keep driving.,d:Find a safe place to stop and take a short nap.
note: When drowsy, stop in a safe place and rest; short naps can restore alertness more effectively than stimulants.

question: What is the best way to avoid hydroplaning in wet conditions?
options: a:Apply the brakes as soon as your car begins to skid.,b:Drive at speeds suitable for ideal conditions.,c:Slow down.
note: Reduce speed in wet conditions to keep tire contact with the road and avoid hydroplaning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a one-way street, you may turn left onto another one-way street only if:
options: a:Traffic on the street you are turning onto moves to the left.,b:Traffic on the street moves to the right.,c:You are turning from the rightmost lane.,d:You increase your speed before turning.
note: Left turns onto one-way streets are allowed only when traffic on the destination street flows left into which you will turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you and the driver on your left reach a four-way stop at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Whoever is signaling to make a turn has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on your left has the right-of-way.,c:You have the right-of-way.
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way; if the other driver is to your left, you go first.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is unlawful when passing another vehicle?
options: a:Pass another vehicle in any marked no passing zone.,b:Pass another vehicle over a railroad crossing.,c:Both of the above.
note: You may not pass at railroad crossings or in marked no-passing zones, on hills, curves, or where visibility is insufficient.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline mean for passing?
options: a:Passing is allowed for drivers with a shoulder lane.,b:Only left turns are permitted across the lines.,c:Passing is prohibited from either direction.,d:Passing is allowed from both directions.
note: A double solid yellow line indicates no vehicle from either direction may cross to pass.

question: Why is driving at night more dangerous than daytime?
options: a:You cannot see as far ahead at night.,b:The road is always more slippery at night.,c:Your reaction time is slower at night.
note: Reduced visibility and glare at night limit how far ahead you can see; use headlights and drive cautiously.

question: When is the most hazardous time to turn or stop in rainy weather?
options: a:During the first half hour of rain.,b:After it has been raining all day.,c:One half hour after the rain stops.,d:When puddles form away from intersections.
note: Road surfaces are slickest during the first 30 minutes of rainfall due to oil and residue mixing with water.

question: Which statement about changing lanes is correct?
options: a:Vehicles with two outside mirrors have no blind spots.,b:You only need to look over your right shoulder for any lane change.,c:Look over the right shoulder for a right lane change and over the left shoulder for a left lane change after checking mirrors.
note: Signal, check mirrors, and glance over the appropriate shoulder to check blind spots before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you not do?
options: a:Continue to the next exit and find an alternate route.,b:Back up on the road or shoulder.,c:Proceed to the next exit
note: Do not back up on the freeway or shoulder—continue to the next exit or follow an alternate route.

question: If you see animals near the roadway while driving, you should:
options: a:Speed up to scare them away.,b:Stop immediately in the travel lane.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.,d:Quickly swerve into the next lane.
note: Animals may suddenly dart into the road; reduce speed and be prepared to stop safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic after parking at a curb, what should you do?
options: a:Wait for the first two vehicles to pass then merge.,b:Drive more slowly than other traffic for 200 feet.,c:Enter immediately and force other drivers to adjust.,d:Wait for a gap large enough to get up to the speed of traffic.
note: When merging from a curb, wait for a gap that allows you to accelerate to the flow of traffic safely.

question: If your wheels run off the pavement onto the shoulder, what should you do first?
options: a:Apply the brakes and turn the front wheels sharply to the left.,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly,c:Turn the front wheels slightly to the left to edge back onto the pavement.
note: If you run off the pavement, stay calm, hold the wheel, lift off the gas, and slow gently before re-entering traffic.

question: Which foot should you use for both braking and accelerating?
options: a:Either foot interchangeably.,b:Your right foot.,c:Your left foot.,d:Both feet simultaneously.
note: Use your right foot for both the brake and accelerator to avoid accidentally pressing both pedals at once.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach a green light but traffic is blocking the intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Honk to make traffic move.,b:Partially enter to establish right-of-way.,c:Continue into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.,d:Do not enter the intersection until you can completely clear it.
note: Even with a green light you must not enter an intersection unless you can clear it fully to avoid blocking cross traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn from a two-way street, where should you position your vehicle?
options: a:Near the right-hand side of the road.,b:On the left of the centerline.,c:Near the centerline.
note: Begin the left turn from the lane nearest the centerline and turn into the first legal lane available without cutting the corner.
